text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys drop opener, 24-20 Sep 04, 2025 at 11:40 PM Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The outcome didn't fall in his favor, but Brian Schottenheimer still had quite the debut as head coach of the Cowboys.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite losing, 24-20, to the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas gave the defending champions all they could handle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In one of the craziest starts to a game you'll ever see, the best player on Philadelphia's defense, Jalen Carter, was ejected before an offensive play was ever run.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: While the Eagles' Ben VanSumeren was being attended to by trainers following an apparent knee injury on the opening kickoff, Carter stepped toward the Cowboys' huddle to have a few words with Dak Prescott.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Philadelphia's star defensive tackle then spit on the Dallas quarterback and was immediately ejected from the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Talk about an unexpected turn of events.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And the Eagles' loss was indeed the Cowboys' gain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas put up points on each of its four possessions in the first half and finished the game with 307 yards of offense to the Eagles' 302.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Schottenheimer tried to use the ground attack more, especially in the first half, as the team went on to total 115 rushing yards overall.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And their only two touchdowns came courtesy of running back Javonte Williams.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But Prescott was the real catalyst for the team's offense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Although he threw for only 188 yards, he completed 61.8 percent of his passes in his first game back after suffering a season-ending hamstring injury in 2024.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: CeeDee Lamb showed he's still one of the best wideouts in the business with 110 receiving yards on seven catches, while George Pickens, in his first game with the Cowboys, totaled 30 receiving yards on three grabs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Unfortunately, when it came to the Dallas defense, Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was the difference in this one.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He put up just 152 yards passing but scrambled through the Cowboys efforts for 62 rushing yards and two scores.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, coming into the game, defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus knew he would have his hands full with running back Saquon Barkley, but the Cowboys held him to only 3.3 yards per carry and 60 rushing yards total.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And Philadelphia's top two receivers, A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith, had just one catch for 8 yards and three catches for 16 yards, respectively.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter Following the shocking ejection of Carter, Prescott quickly led his team 53 yards in six plays to the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: His first completion of the season was to the newcomer Pickens for 6 yards, which was followed two snaps later by 32-yard completion to Lamb that set the Cowboys up with first-and-goal at the Eagles' 1-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Williams then scored the touchdown to give the visitors an early lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But Hurts and company responded with a 10-play, 70-yard drive of their own that quickly evened the score, 7-7.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Philly's quarterback completed all three of his passes for 33 yards and scrambled the last 4 yards untouched across the goal line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter The Cowboys found themselves with a first-and-goal at the Eagles' 1-yard line when the second quarter got underway.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This came largely thanks to a pair of passes to Lamb for a combined 44 yards, as well as a 34-yard pass interference penalty on Philadelphia that dug Dallas out of a second-and-23 hole.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That left it to Williams, who added an 11-yard run and then wrapped up the drive with another bull-rush into across the goal line to put the Cowboys back in front.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Hurts, though, continued to be elusive as Dallas' blow was met by a counterstrike by the home side.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of the 65 yards the Eagles picked up on their next possession, Hurts accounted for 49 of them through a combination of passing the ball and running with it.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The last eight of those yards came when he again escaped the pocket and raced to the left pylon for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas kept the pressure on, but this time managed only three points.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Brandon Aubrey picked up right where he left off from his Pro Bowl campaign in 2024, splitting the uprights from 41 yards out.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, in this game against this Eagles offense, field goals weren't going to do it.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And sure enough, Philadelphia quickly marched 81 yards in just 1:43 of clock to take a 21-17 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Dallas defense continued its struggles to contain Hurts, although the big blow was a 51-yard pass to wideout Jahan Dotson on third-and-6.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Barkley eventually finished the series with a 10-yard run up the middle for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But getting the ball back with 44 seconds left in the half, Schottenheimer and Prescott worked the two-minute offense to perfection, as the latter completed all five of his pass attempts to get his team to the Philadelphia 35-yard line with 4 seconds on the clock.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That was enough time for Aubrey, whose field goal was good from 53 yards to make the score a tight 21-20 at the half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter The Dallas defense got a win of sorts to start the second half as they held Philadelphia to a mere field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: An 8-yard sack of Hurts by Marshawn Kneeland stalled the Eagles' drive, but Jake Elliott's 58-yard field goal tacked on another three points, upping the advantage to 24-20.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And then disaster struck.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Led by a Miles Sanders run of 49 yards and an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty by Philadelphia on third-and-22, the Cowboys had a first down at the Eagles' 11.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But that's when Sanders had the ball stripped on a rush up the middle, and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell scooped up the fumble before being tripped up on perhaps a touchdown-saving tackle by Prescott (the first tackle of his career).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Regardless, that brought an end to the Dallas threat.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Maybe the Cowboys caught a break, though, when whatever momentum the Eagles may have had was stunted when the turnover was immediately followed by a weather delay due to lightning in the area.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After a stoppage that lasted just over an hour, the Cowboys defense came out and forced the game's first punt of the night.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter With both offenses struggling to find any rhythm after the break, the defenses took centerstage with the two sides trading punts through most of the final frame.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Then with 3:02 remaining, Prescott and the offense took the field at their own 18-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And after a 15-yard completion to Pickens on the left sideline, Prescott found Lamb deep over the middle, only to have the ball bounce off the receiver's hands, incomplete.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Three snaps later, on fourth-and-10 at the Dallas 45-yard line, Prescott lofted another pass to Lamb down the left side, but the receiver couldn't haul in what would have been a sensational diving catch.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Instead, the Cowboys turned the ball over on downs with only 1:54 on the clock.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And after picking up a first down of their own, Philadelphia was then able to run out the clock, game over.

text: September 05, 2025 Eagles vs. Cowboys Week 1 observations: Pass offense looks the same, defense made big stops, Eagles win another opener Eagles defensive tackles work overtime, Saquon Barkley still carried a heavy workload, Quinyon Mitchell traveled and other observations from the By Geoff Mosher PhillyVoice Staff Eagles NFL Colleen Claggett/for PhillyVoice Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles tackles George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys during a NFL football game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on September 4, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

text: Read More Everything seemed perfect at the Linc.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fireworks lit the sky.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A championship banner was unfurled.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "Jump Around" blared over the loudspeaker.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Chants of "Dallas Sucks" soon reverberated around the sold-out stadium.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was a perfect Thursday evening for the Eagles and their fans – and then came kickoff.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Ben VanSumeren went down on the opening kick, and while the medical staff helped him into a cart, flags flew as Jalen Carter had spit on Dak Prescott to get ejected before the teams could huddle up for the first offensive snap.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Then the Cowboys went 53 yards and scored a touchdown for the early lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And then the game just got weird.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Personal fouls kept coming.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jalen Hurts burned the Cowboys with long runs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: CeeDee Lamb burned the Eagles because he's CeeDee Lamb.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Miles Sanders came back to haunt the Eagles with a 49-yard run, then came back to help the Eagles by fumbling.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Lightning caused a long delay.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In the end, the Eagles held onto to win, 24-20, after Lamb failed to corral a deep ball on 4th-and-3 with less than 2 minutes to play after sprawling out and taking a little contact from Cooper DeJean.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Here's a whole bunch of interesting observations, notes and nuggets from a weird, wild NFL opener...

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The defensive interior played a whole lot The byproduct of Jalen Carter's ejection wasn't just leaving the Eagles without their best overall lineman but also forced Jordan Davis and Moro Ojomo into barely leaving the field.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They held up in the first half but Dallas tried came out in the second half with a ground-and-pound approach, running on its first three plays and four of the first five, the fourth being Miles Sanders' 49-yard scamper down the left side.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But as the Eagles know too well, Sanders can giveth and taketh away.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The former Eagles running back's fumble three plays later – caused by Byron Young and Jihaad Campbell – saved the Eagles from falling behind again.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: the lightning delay might have actually helped the d-linemen recharge as the defense came up with some critical fourth-quarter four-man rushes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It didn't appear that Vic Fangio blitzed very much, although he threw a timely blitz on that final pass from Prescott to Lamb that fell incomplete.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The pass offense showed some evolution but was it better?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Right from the start, the Eagles showed a ton of motion, shifting, even some misdirection as Kevin Patullo made his debut as offensive coordinator.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It's funny, because that was supposed to be Kellen Moore's thing, but Moore eventually ditched a lot of that stuff and went more basic.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Patullo is benefitting by being with the team since Nick Sirianni arrived in 2021, so plenty of experience with Hurts, and also from an offense that replaced just one starter, on the o-line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the fourth offensive snap, the Eagles aligned three tights on the right side of the line and then ran a left-side pitch to Saquon Barkley that went for 16 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Eagles talked a lot about evolving as an offense, and being a new iteration, and it certainly was on display for the opener.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But overall, the results of the pass game didn't look very different.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A.J. Brown was basically invisible, so was DeVonta Smith against a Dallas secondary that had guys who missed a whole lot of time in camp.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That was a vintage Jalen Hurts/Eagles offense game I actually wrote in my notebook when Hurts completed consecutive passes inside the hashes to Dallas Goedert – not his strongest asset – on the Eagles' second possession, and then was vintage Hurts a few plays later by ignoring A.J. Brown crossing inside the 5-yard-line and just running in an 8-yard TD.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: All of Hurts' best attributes were on display early – signature third-down runs and a beautiful deep ball to Jahan Dotson down the right seam that Dotson caught in stride for 51 yards – on 3rd-and-6.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Not a lot of QBs make that decision on 3rd-and-6.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In the second half, not so much as the Eagles punted on two of their first three possessions after the break and then gave the ball bacl to Dallas with about three minutes to go in the fourth after another 3-and-out.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Quinyon Mitchell shadowed, but the CB2 battle wasn't encouraging We didn't have to wait very long for two things – Vic Fangio using Quinyon Mitchell in shadow coverage, and for Fangio to get tired of Adoree' Jackson.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Mitchell shadowed George Pickens for the game – he won more than he lost and held Pickens in check – but Jackson struggled against CeeDee Lamb, who mainly lined up to the field or slot as he typically does.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Lamb had four catches for 86 yards in the first half, and Fangio went to Jakorian Bennett on Dallas' fourth possession.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He was immediately flagged for DPI, on his very first Eagles snap.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A few plays later, he got beat by Lamb on a 10-yard slant to get Dallas into field goal position with 15 seconds to go in the half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jackson was back to start the second half, left briefly in the second half to get evalauted for a concussion but returned after the lightning delay.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Interestingly, Mitchell didn't cover Pickens on 3rd-and-5 late in the fourth, and Dak Prescott went right to Pickens for a 15-yard catch.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys missed Micah Parsons (duh)

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But actually more for his experience than his pass rush acumen.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Hurts capitalized on Dallas' young edge rushers, who got way too north and too wide with their rush lanes early in the game, giving Hurts plenty of green to expose with his legs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two of the Eagles' first three third-down conversions came via Hurts escaping the pocket and moving the sticks with his legs, including his TD run on the opening drive and a 15-yarder on 3rd-and-5 on the second drive, and then again a few plays later on his 8-yard TD run.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Cowboys defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus made some adjustments after the break, sending more pressure but also scheming to keep Hurts in the pocket, which led to Hurts getting sacked by Marshawn Kneeland and then getting hit on a hurried incomplete pass on the Eagles' opening possession of the third, leading to a Jake Elliott 58-yarder – the first Eagles possession that didn't result in a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Did the Eagles "lighten Saquon's load?"

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: What do you think?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He had 12 touches in the first half (10 runs, two receptions on three targets) and finished with 21 in total – a pace for 357 touches over 17 games if you're into math.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It probably didn't help that Will Shipley left with a concussion and Ben VanSumeren was injured on the opening kick, but the Eagles will give Barkley the ball when the game is tight, and there was never a moment when the game wasn't tight.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And given the schedule, they'll probably be in a bunch of tight games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If BenVanSumeren is out for long again, it'll hurt I'm still convinced the Eagles hid their intentions for Ben VanSumeren's role in the offense in the preseason, and now we might never know what those plans were if VanSumeren is out for the season, or just for a really long time.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Eagles occasionally used Kylen Granson in an H-back type role, and Granson has some catch-and-run abilities, but any extended VanSumeren absence will probably force the Eagles to ditch that role and go with more basic two tight-end formations.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Vic Fangio clearly doesn't prefer a deep EDGE rotation Last year, Fangio had no problem relying on Josh Sweat, Nolan Smith and Jalyx Hunt to handle the majority of EDGE snaps after Bryce Huff was rendered a) ineffective and b) injured, and after Brandon Graham went down with a torn triceps.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It appears Fangio just doesn't feel like he needs a Jim Schwartzian type of edge rotation, because Azeez Ojulari was a surprise inactive, leaving Fangio to lean heavily on Smith, Hunt and Josh Uche.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The pass rush had some moments, but Prescott generally didn't face a ton of pressure.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Once again, Fangio showed that he doesn't care about someone's contract.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Ojulari signed a one-year deal for $4 million this offseason while Uche inked a 1-year deal with $1.25 million guaranteed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys

text: Presented by Instant Analysis: Giants fall to Cowboys 40-37 in OT thriller Sep 15, 2025 at 09:00 AM Dan Salomone Senior Managing Editor, Giants.com Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: AT A GLANCE Fourteen penalties for 160 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Russell Wilson moonballs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jaxson Dart's first NFL action.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Seven second-half lead changes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Forty-one combined points in the fourth quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants' annual trip to Dallas had a little bit of everything, but they couldn't come away with the most important thing in a 40-37 overtime loss, dropping them to 0-2 to start the season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Wilson threw a go-ahead, 48-yard touchdown to Malik Nabers with 25 seconds left in the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas responded and set up a 64-yard field goal attempt by Brandon Aubrey, which he made as time expired to force overtime.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants won the overtime coin toss and elected to play defense first.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They forced Dallas to punt, setting up a score-and-win situation.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After both sides punted again, Wilson tried to find Nabers deep one more time, but Donovan Wilson intercepted the pass.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the ensuing possession, Dak Prescott scrambled for 14 yards to set up Aubrey's 46-yard, game-winning field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: UP NEXT After starting the season with back-to-back road games in the NFC East, the Giants (0-2) will open their 2025 home schedule with consecutive games against interconference opponents.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First up is the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Chiefs lost their season opener to the Los Angeles Chargers, who will travel to MetLife Stadium in Week 4.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: WHAT WE LEARNED ABOUT THE OFFENSE Andrew Thomas, the Giants' starting left tackle, has not played since he suffered a season-ending foot injury on Oct. 13, 2024.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Thomas continues to do more in practice each week, including taking team reps, but was listed as doubtful on the final injury report – and ultimately ruled out on gameday – in Weeks 1 and 2.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: His replacement, James Hudson III, was called for four penalties on the opening possession in Dallas and held back an otherwise promising drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Devin Singletary took the first carry of the game and Cam Skattebo had the second.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Tyrone Tracy Jr. handled the third for nine yards before breaking a 24-yarder, but it was called back by a holding penalty on wide receiver Darius Slayton.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A 10-yard run by the rookie Skattebo was then called back on a personal foul by Hudson, who followed it up with a false start.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Then Russell Wilson connected with wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson for a 50-yard gain (longest of Robinson's career), minus 15 yards due to an unnecessary roughness penalty on Hudson.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In total, the Giants' first drive – which began with a negated 67-yard kickoff return due to a holding penalty and ended with a short field goal – included six penalties.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It spanned 16 plays for 60 yards in just under nine minutes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rookie Marcus Mbow, a fifth-round pick out of Purdue who had an impressive preseason, replaced Hudson on the Giants' second drive, which began with a false start penalty on tight end Daniel Bellinger.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Similarly, it ended with another short field goal and a 6-0 Giants lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants pushed through the penalty problem and scored their first touchdown of the season on a 29-yard pass from Wilson to Malik Nabers, who made a sensational catch over two-time Pro Bowl cornerback Trevon Diggs in the end zone with 5:37 left in the second quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants totaled just 231 yards in Week 1 but eclipsed that mark by halftime against the Cowboys.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Wilson completed 30 of 41 passes for a career-high 450 yards and three touchdowns with one interception and a 123.0 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 235 yards in the first half were the most by a Giants quarterback since Eli Manning had 236 against the Eagles on Nov. 25, 2018.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Last week, Wilson completed just 45.9 percent of his passes with a 59.3 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Robinson posted a personal-best 142 receiving yards on eight catches (17.8-yard average) and a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Not to be outdone, Nabers finished with nine receptions for 167 yards, second-most of his career, and two touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite all the yards, the Giants did struggle again in the red zone as they couldn't find the end zone on four of their five drives inside the 20.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jaxson Dart made his NFL debut with 12:51 left in a game that had the Cowboys leading 20-16.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: From the Dallas 25, Dart handed the ball off to Skattebo, who burst straight up the middle for 24 yards down to the goal line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The fellow rookie then punched it in on the next play as the Giants regained a three-point lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the Cowboys retook the lead, Dart returned for two more plays on the Giants' next drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He handed the ball off to Tracy for a first down on second-and-short.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dart then lost three yards on a run.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nabers couldn't hold onto a third-and-four pass that would have provided a fresh set of downs with 2:50 left in the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nevertheless, on fourth-and-four, Wilson then threw a 32-yard touchdown to Robinson on the very next play to put the Giants back up by three points.

text: The Giants were down two linebackers (Micah McFadden and Demetrius Flannigan-Fowles) and a defensive lineman (Rakeem Nuñez-Roches Sr.).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: McFadden was quickly ruled out last week after being carted off with a foot injury in the season opener.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He was later placed on injured reserve.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Flannigan-Fowles was also ruled out after he aggravated a calf injury in practice this week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He did not make the trip with the team to Dallas.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nuñez-Roches was doubtful with a foot injury.

text: Cor'Dale

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Flott has seemingly cemented his starting spot at cornerback opposite Paulson Adebo.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Flott broke up two passes and made a critical play at the end of the first half, keeping tight end Jake Ferguson inbounds with the clocking winding down.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dak Prescott rushed everyone to the line, but CeeDee Lamb was called for a false start to end the second quarter with the Giants ahead 13-10.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants made a key play at a similar point in the game a week ago at Washington, where Abdul Carter forced Jayden Daniels into an intentional grounding that kept the Commanders from adding points before heading to the locker room.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants had three sacks in a Week 1 game for the first time since 2011 and followed it up with three more on Sunday.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Brian Burns, who had two in the opener, notched his third of the young season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Kayvon Thibodeaux also took down Dak Prescott, who entered Sunday with a 13-game winning streak over the Giants as a starter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nickel cornerback Dru Phillips notched the Giants' first takeaway of the season, intercepting Prescott's pass intended for Lamb on the opening drive of the second half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas took its first lead of the game on Javonte Williams' 30-yard touchdown run with 7:20 left in the third quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the previous play, Phillips was called for a 22-yard passing interference penalty.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Linebacker Darius Muasau, who stepped up in place of McFadden, left in the third quarter with a concussion.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Burns then played some off-ball linebacker and quickly delivered a big hit on Javonte Williams for a tackle for loss.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the Giants regained the lead with 2:44 left, the Cowboys responded with an 11-play, 71-yard drive that ended with a go-ahead, six-yard touchdown catch by George Pickens with 52 seconds remaining.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: To start overtime, the Giants forced the Cowboys to punt, setting up a score-and-win opportunity for the offense.

text: New this season, the dead ball spot of a touchback if the ball lands in the end zone and is downed in the end zone by the receiving team is now the 35-yard line (it was the 30 in 2024).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The "dynamic kickoff" is designed to promote more returns and resemble a play from scrimmage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The kickoff return rate around the NFL in Week 1 (75.6 percent) more than doubled the rate from the 2024 opening slate of games (33.3 percent).

text: A 67-yard return by Gunner Olszewski on the opening kickoff the game was negated by a holding penalty on linebacker Swayze Bozeman, who was activated from the practice squad on Saturday.

text: Graham Gano made all three of his field goal attempts with a long of 38 yards.

text: GIANTS New York Giants fall to Dallas Cowboys, 40-37, in overtime thriller Dan Benton Giants Wire Updated Sept. 14, 2025, 4:52 p.m. ET The New York Giants (0-1) traveled to AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, to take on the Dallas Cowboys (0-1) in a Week 2 NFC East clash.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In a game that was expected to be a blowout, the Giants and Cowboys put on a dazzling display, exchanging blows like heavyweight boxers until the final minutes of overtime.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If not for the penalties (26 combined), the game would have been considered an instant classic.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Alas, the Giants could not come up with the knockout blow and fell to the Cowboys for the 16th time in their last 17 meetings.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Cowboys win in OT, 40-37 Sep 14, 2025 at 04:08 PM

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This game sure looked ugly at times, but in the end, it was a thing of beauty for the Cowboys and their fans … thanks to Brandon Aubrey.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas' Pro Bowl kicker tied the game as time expired with a 64-yard field goal and then won it in overtime with a 46-yarder as the clock hit zeroes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, Dallas avoided the franchise's first tie since 1969 and took down the rival Giants, 40-37, to move to 1-1 on the season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite the visitors racking up 14 penalties, tied for the second most by an opponent in Cowboys history, for 160 yards, the third-highest total in club record books, Dallas couldn't take advantage of New York's undisciplined play.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In fact, the visitors' self-inflicted wounds may have been the difference in this close affair, although the Cowboys had 12 penalties for 106 yards of their own.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dak Prescott was again sharp, completing 73.1 percent of passes for 361 yards, two touchdowns and an interception to earn a 96.7 rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: CeeDee Lamb posted 113 receiving yards, while Jake Ferguson added 78 and George Pickens another 68, plus his first touchdown wearing the Star.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And on the ground, Javonte Williams continued to shine, totaling 97 rushing yards, which included a 30-yard touchdown run.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overall, Dallas ran for 135 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Meanwhile, on the other side of the ball, New York quarterback Russell Wilson largely picked apart the Cowboys defense, completing 73.2 percent of his passes for 450 yards with three touchdowns and one interception to post a 123.0 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas had trouble containing star wideout Malik Nabors, who collected 167 receiving yards and two touchdowns, but slot receiver Wan'Dale Robinson also proved to be a problem as he finished the day with a career-high 142 receiving yards and a score of his own.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys, though, did sack the quarterback three times and got an all-important turnover when they perhaps needed it most.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overall, the Cowboys totaled 478 yards of offense with a time of possession of 37:21.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They were also 3 for 3 in the red zone, compared to the Giants' finishing 1 for 5.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: New York picked up 506 yards of offense on the day while holding onto the ball for 32:39 First Quarter As much as the Giants tried to derail themselves on the first drive of the game – committing six penalties, including one on the opening kickoff – they still managed to reel off 16 plays and eat 8:49 off the clock to reach the Cowboys' 20-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But there the drive would end, so even though Wilson threw for 95 yards during the possession, New York had to settle for a 38-yard field goal for an early 3-0 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two drives, six points for the Giants.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys had to punt on their first series after failing to snap what would have been a successful conversion on fourth-and-1 before the play-clock hit zero.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, the visitors then went 55 yards in eight plays before Graham Gano kicked a 33-yard field goal for New York.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter The offense finally showed some life as the second quarter got underway, Prescott connecting with CeeDee Lamb for a nice 34-yard gain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But on third-and-10 at the Giants' 25-yard line, the quarterback was sacked, so the Cowboys turned to Brandon Aubrey, who was good from 51 yards to get Dallas on the board.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Unfortunately, the Giants then needed only five plays to score the game's first touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The damage was done when Wilson found Wan'Dale Robinson for 25 yards to the Dallas 29 and then connected with Malik Nabers in the end zone on the very next play, New York improving their stake to 13-3.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But the Cowboys responded with an eight-play, 64-yard drive to pay dirt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: While things took a laughable turn when four penalties, three on the Giants, were called on one play, Dallas got the touchdown on the next snap when Prescott threw a dart to KaVonte Turpin in the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas had one more chance, getting the ball back with 1:36 remaining in the half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With no timeouts, though, the home team was unable to get into field goal range and so found themselves still trailing, 13-10, at the break.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter Whatever momentum the Cowboys might have eked out in the second quarter quickly came to an end as the third frame got underway.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two plays into the half, Prescott tried to find Lamb across the middle, but throwing off his back foot, instead had hit pass picked off.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Set up with great field position at the Dallas 40-yard line, the Giants did get down to the 10.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, on fourth-and-3, running back Cam Skattebo couldn't corral Wilson's pass, so with the incompletion, the Cowboys luckily came away unscathed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And this time they took advantage as Dallas went 90 yards in just six plays for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Helped by roughing the passer and pass interference penalties that provided 37 yards, the Cowboys saw running back Javonte Williams pick up the final 30 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He powered through the line of scrimmage with some tough rushing, broke a couple of tackles and then went untouched the final 20 yards to the end zone, which gave the Cowboys their first lead of the game, 17-13.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants narrowed it to a one-point game with a 33-yard field, thanks mainly to a 52-yard completion from Wilson to Darious Slayton.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But Dallas defense wouldn't let New York get past the 10-yard line, limiting the harm.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter You kick a field goal; we'll kick a field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: As the clock ticked over into the final quarter, the Cowboys were in the midst of an 11-play, 56-yard drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But they couldn't finish off the possession, instead settling for a 44-yard Aubrey field goal to go back up by four.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Less than two minutes of game clock later, though, Dallas again saw itself trailing on the scoreboard.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This time it was the Cowboys who helped the other side with a costly penalty, as a pass interference call on safety Donovan Wilson resulted in a 21-yard penalty down to the Dallas 25-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The battering ram Skattebo then did the rest, rumbling 24 yards to the 1-yard line before picking up the final distance on the next play to put the Giants in front, 23-20.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That lead didn't last long.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott was firing on all cylinders on his team's next series, completing each of his five passes for 60 yards, while Miles Sanders bounced in at running back and finished off the drive with runs of 6 and 4 yards to reach the end zone, Dallas back on top 27-23.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And then disaster struck.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On fourth-and-4 at the Dallas 32-yard line, Wilson found Robinson streaking wide open down the right seem, the slot receiver hauling in the pass in the end zone to put the Giants back on top, 30-27, with 2:44 left in the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But that was plenty of time for Prescott and company to go to work.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They needed only 1:52 of clock time and 71 yards in 11 plays, to get the home team back on top.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Spreading the ball around, the Cowboys' quarterback found Jalen Tolber for 11 yards, Pickens for 14 and Lamb for 12 with Williams rushing for 13 as well.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In the end, it was Pickens who got the scoring honors, hauling in Prescott's offering just inside the left pylon for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Now with only 48 seconds remaining, the game seemed to be in hand.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But Wilson had other ideas.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He scrambled 15 yards to the Dallas 48-yard line, which set him up for a deep ball to Nabers, who with two Cowboys defenders on him, hauled in the bomb in the end zone for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Thirty-three seconds were left when the Cowboys took the field one last time.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And an 18-yard pass to Jake Ferguson set Dallas up at the New York 49-yard line with 9 seconds left.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In somewhat surprising move, Brian Schottenheimer called a quick handoff to Williams to simply set Aubrey up for a 64-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And the sure-footed kicker was good, slipping the ball through the uprights to tie the score, 37-37, and send the game into overtime.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 41 points posted in the final frame tied the Cowboys' team record for the most scored by both teams combined in the fourth quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overtime The Giants won the toss but chose to let the Cowboys take the field first on offense, but neither side could do anything on their first possessions of the extra time.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: So when Dallas then got the ball back a second time, any points would decide the game, a true sudden death.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But while the Cowboys had to punt again, they got the ball back with two minutes remaining.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Russell Wilson attempted a deep ball to Nabers, only to have safety Donovan Wilson intercept the pass to give Dallas the ball at its own 30-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott made it count.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: His first pass was a 27-yarder to Pickens to get into enemy territory.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two plays later, Prescott escaped the pocket and scramble up the middle 14 yards to the Giants 28.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That left it to Aubrey, who came on with 4 seconds left to try a 46-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And, of course, Aubrey was money, providing the needed three points to send the fans home happy with a 40-37 victory.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Where to begin?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: To answer that question, it is best to start at the end of the third game in NFL history to go to overtime after each team scored at least 20 points in the fourth quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: THE GAME WAS OVER WHEN… Brandon Aubrey kicked a 46-yard field goal attempt as time expired, giving the Cowboys a 40-37 win in the first overtime game in the series since Oct. 16, 2005 at Texas Stadium.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Coincidentally, it was also the last time the Giants played a noon local time game at Dallas.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Both teams were in a next-score-wins scenario after trading punts to start overtime, following the wake of a fourth quarter that produced 41 combined points.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That's when the Giants turned the ball over for the first time this season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Russell Wilson, looking to add to his 450-yard, three-touchdown game with another moonball to Malik Nabers, dropped back to the Giants' 20 and launched it 50 yards downfield to a waiting safety, Donovan Wilson.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: George Pickens started off the ensuing – and decisive – possession with a 27-yard gain off a pass from Dak Prescott.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two plays later, the quarterback scrambled up the middle for 14 yards to the Giants' 28 and set up the game-winner for Aubrey, who also forced overtime with a 64-yard field goal at the end of regulation.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: According to NFL Research, the six lead changes in the fourth quarter and overtime are tied for the most in a game in NFL history (Vikings vs. Ravens in Week 14, 2013).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "Every game's different," coach Brian Daboll said in his postgame press conference.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "Last week, it's 14-6 in the fourth quarter with seven minutes left.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This game is back-and-forth with 24 seconds left.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Kick off.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: We knew Aubrey had a long leg.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Got to play tight coverage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Got to do some things rush-wise.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Made some good plays.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They just made one more play than we did.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: YOU HAVE TO SEE THIS…AND THIS…AND THIS You had to see all of it to believe it, but the chain of events in the fourth quarter also included Jaxson Dart's NFL debut.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 25 th overall pick entered with 12:51 left in a game that had the Cowboys leading 20-16.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: From the Dallas 25, Dart handed the ball off to Cam Skattebo, another rookie, who burst straight up the middle for 24 yards down to the goal line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Skattebo then punched it in on the next play as the Giants regained a three-point lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Daboll wasn't done with the wrinkle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the Cowboys regained the lead, Dart returned for two more plays on the Giants' next drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He handed the ball off to Tyrone Tracy Jr. for a first down, converting a second-and-short.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dart then lost three yards on a run.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Wilson re-entered, and Nabers couldn't hold onto a third-and-four pass that would have provided a fresh set of downs with 2:50 left in the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nevertheless, on fourth-and-four, Wilson then threw a 32-yard touchdown to Wan'Dale Robinson on the very next play to put the Giants back up by three points.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "Well, the one that we hit with Skat, we were just talking about our sideline," Daboll said of playing Dart in that moment.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "We didn't have much going in the running game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A couple of plays here or there.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That particular one is kind of 11-on-11 football with a read.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Kind of sprung Skat.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was good blocking, so, they did a couple of good jobs with the handoff and then he kept one and then slipped on one.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: I think that was right before the fourth down if I'm not mistaken but that was the reason why."

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: STAT OF THE GAME The Giants more than doubled their offensive output from Week 1 (231 yards at Washington, 506 at Dallas) despite being penalized 14 times for 160 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 37 points were the third-highest total of the Daboll era (since 2022) and could have been more.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants were 1-for-5 in the red zone after going 0-for-2 in Week 1.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys, meanwhile, found the end zone on all three of their trips inside the 20.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "Far too many," Daboll said of the penalties.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: "I wanted the guys to play physical this game, be aggressive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Roughing the passer, DPI.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: There were a lot of penalties called this game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Almost 260 yards worth between two teams.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: We certainly don't want to have that many penalties."

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The penalties became a storyline early in the game when James Hudson III, who has been filling in for Andrew Thomas, was called for four penalties on the opening drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rookie Marcus Mbow, a fifth-round pick out of Purdue who had an impressive preseason, took over from there.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: NOTABLE Wilson completed 30 of 41 passes (73.2 percent) for 450 yards, three touchdowns, one interception and a quarterback rating of 123.0.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 450 passing yards are the second-most in his career and tied for the fourth-highest total in franchise history.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Eli Manning also threw for that total at Dallas in the 2013 season opener.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Robinson finished with eight catches and a career-high 142 yards and one touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the opening possession of the game, Robinson caught a 50-yard pass, the longest reception of his career.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nabers totaled nine catches for 167 yards and two touchdowns, the fourth 100-yard receiving game and third multi-touchdown game of his career.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: His second touchdown – which went for 48 yards – was part of sequence that included a combined two touchdowns and one field goal in the final 52 seconds of regulation.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: QUOTABLE "I love watching people be relentless.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: I love watching boxing, for example…you know, we're in a 17-round fight.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: We battled in the first round and second round.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: We've got more to do.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: So, I was just proud of how we needed to be able to answer the way we did.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: I've been a part of a lot of crazy games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: I don't know if I've ever been part of one that crazy with that much grit."

text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys fall to Bears, 31-14 Sep 21, 2025 at 06:36 PM

text: Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the New York Giants torched the Dallas defense last weekend, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the problems in the secondary could be easily fixed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Needless to say, they still have plenty of work to do as quarterback Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears dismantled the Cowboys defense in a 31-14 victory.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The loss dropped Dallas to 1-2 on the young season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Adding injury to insult, the Cowboys also lost starting wide receiver CeeDee Lamb in the first quarter due to an ankle injury.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He attempted to come back in the second quarter, but left after one play, his day done.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And he wasn't the only one banged up.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Trevon Diggs (shoulder) and Kenny Clark (ankle), both key members of the defense, were also sidelined in the fourth quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Even with those two, however, the Cowboys simply had no answer for Williams as he threw for 298 yards and tied his career high with four touchdown passes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He also wasn't sacked once and had no interceptions for a 142.6 passer rating, a personal best.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Eight different players hauled in passes for the Bears, although Luther Burden led the way with three catches for 101 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the other side of the ball, quarterback Dak Prescott completed 77.5 percent of his passes for 251 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for an 80.3 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jake Ferguson was the primary target on the receiving end, totaling a career-high 13 catches, which is the most by a tight end in the NFL this season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He had 82 receiving yards while George Pickens, stepping into the No. 1 wideout role for Lamb, finished with 68 receiving yards and a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys did see success on the ground as Javonte Williams averaged 7.6 yards per carry on his way to 76 rushing yards overall.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, once the deficit became too large, Dallas basically had to abandon the run.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter How quickly the momentum can turn.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys forced a three-and-out on Chicago's opening offensive possession, and then on their first try quickly worked out to the 50-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Things really looked good when Williams took off around the left end for 22 yards to the Bears' 28-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But that's when Chicago cornerback Tyrique Stevenson came up behind Williams and ripped the ball away for essentially a fumble recovery.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, the Bears only needed five plays to reach the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Caleb Williams connected with a wide-open Rome Odunze, who had gotten behind the defense after Diggs slipped.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The receiver raced untouched 35 yards to get the home team on the board first, 7-0.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Perhaps even worse, on the fourth play of Dallas' next series, Lamb had to leave the game when his left ankle and leg was rolled up on during a tackle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But at least the Cowboys finished the drive with some positive vibes as Brandon Aubrey picked up right where he left off from last week's heroic performance by kicking a 53-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Unfortunately, the Dallas secondary picked up right where it left off last week as well.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the Giant's Russell Wilson threw several deep passes for scores against the Cowboys, Williams got his second of the game with a flea-flicker that saw him connect with Burden for a 65-yard touchdown to increase Chicago's lead to 14-3.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter Looking to right the ship, the Cowboys offense found itself on the Bears' 13-yard line when the second frame got underway.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But Dallas couldn't finish off the 10-play drive in the end zone so settled for another Aubrey field goal, this one from 33 yards out.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was something to build on, though, and Prescott kept the momentum going on his team's next possession as he was good on all four of his pass attempts, including a 21-yarder to Pickens.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That pair also capped the 57-yard drive with a 2-yard completion that saw the wideout make a one-handed catch for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Going for two, Prescott then zipped a pass to Jalen Tolbert in the middle of the end zone to tie the game, 14-14.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, things didn't get any easier for the Dallas defense as Chicago finished the first half by adding 10 more points.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Coordinator Matt Eberflus' group looked in good shape with the Bears facing third-and-9 at their own 36-yard line, but a screen pass to D'Andre Swift gained 41 yards and an end-around run by receiver Olamide Zaccheaus added another 12 to suddenly put Chicago on the Dallas 11-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: There the defense stood its ground, limiting the damage by forcing the Bears to kick a 30-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But the Cowboys couldn't stop Williams and his offense on their next series.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Starting at its own 29-yard line, Chicago went the distance in seven plays with the quarterback completing passes of 13 and 29 yards before finishing things off with a 10-yard completion to tight end Cole Kmet for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, the Bears went into the break with a 24-14 advantage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter It was more of the same as the second half got underway.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the Cowboys had to punt, the Bears went on a methodical march down the field, eating up nearly 10 minutes off the clock while driving 76 yards in an incredible 19 plays.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: At one point, Chicago reeled off 11 consecutive run plays as Dallas began to wear down.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The drive eventually ended with Chicago going for it on fourth-and-4 at the Cowboys' 4-yard line, and Williams found D.J. Moore standing alone in the back of the end zone for the touchdown and an insurmountable 31-14 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And just like the Dallas offense sustained a crucial injury, now the team's defense was hurting.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Both Diggs, who was questionable to play in the game, and Clark were sidelined during the series.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter Things just went from bad to worse.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the Cowboys' ensuing series, Prescott again had the offense on the move, reaching the Bears' 36-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But a pass to Pickens went off the receiver's hands and into the diving arms of Chicago linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the threat coming to an end.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys, at least, kept fighting on offense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott led his troops all the way down to the Bears' 1-yard line, a 37-yard pass to KaVontae Turpin the big gain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But on fourth-and-goal, Prescott's pass under pressure was picked off in the end zone by Edmunds, Dallas unable to make the final score more reasonable.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, Prescott's day was done as Joe Milton came on for his first action with the Cowboys.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He rifled darts to Pickens for 24 yards, wideout Ryan Flournoy for another 11 and what would have been a 38-yarder to tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford, although the latter was negated due to a penalty.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, it was all for naught as Dallas again got inside the red zone but couldn't get across the goal line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In a fitting end, Milton threw an interception himself to close out a tough day for the Cowboys.

text: GIANTS New York Giants' Jaxson Dart picks up first career win, but it came at a cost

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dan Benton Giants Wire Updated Sept. 28, 2025, 4:29 p.m. ET The New York Giants (1-3) picked up an upset victory over the Los Angeles Chargers (3-1) at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday afternoon -- the first of their season and the first for rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart, who made his starting debut.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Unfortunately for the Giants, the game was overshadowed by a devastating injury to superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers, who is feared to have suffered a season-ending torn ACL in the second quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He was carted off and is scheduled for an MRI on Monday.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dart's play was a bit mixed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He showed flashes at times, but also appeared to lack trust in certain throws, ultimately leaving yards, first downs, and points on the board.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But there was a lot to live and a lot to build on, albeit without Nabers.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In the end, it was the defense -- namely, linebacker Brian Burns -- who got things done and slowed down the high-powered Chargers offense, led by quarterback Justin Herbert.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Burns' late fourth-quarter sack ultimately sealed the game for Big Blue.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Here's how it all went down:

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Final score: Giants 21, Chargers 18 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 Final Giants 7 6 8 0 21 Chargers 0 10 8 0 18 Burns with the big play With the Chargers facing a third-and-9 with roughly 3:00 remaining in the game, linebacker Brian Burns came up with the clutch play: A 16-yard sack of Justin Herbert.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The sack forced a punt and gave the Giants the ball back deep in their territory.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Deadzone With an opportunity to put the game away, the Giants could not capitalize, getting stood up in the redzone once again.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With four plays inside the 10-yard line, the Giants could only get as far as the 1-yard line before a negative Jaxson Dart run and a dropped pass by Wan'Dale Robinson in the endzone (contested) turned the ball over on downs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Chargers storm back It took the Chargers just 1:22 to answer back after the Giants took a 21-10 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They drove 66 yards on three plays, capped off by a 54-yard touchdown courtesy of rookie running back Omarion Hampton.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Like the Giants, Los Angeles then punched in a two-point conversion.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 21, Chargers 18 Dart first career TD Capitalizing on the Dru Phillips interception and finally scoring in the redzone, Giants rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart connected with tight end Theo Johnson for his first career touchdown -- a shovel pass.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It wasn't pretty, but it got the job done.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants then converted a two-point conversion with a Cam Skattebo rush up the middle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 21, Chargers 10 Dru Phillips interception Cornerback Dru Phillips overcame an offensive pass interference to snag a sliding interception off the arm of Justin Herbert with 3:33 remaining in the third quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He returned it 56 yards to the three-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was Phillips' second interception of the year and the Giants' second of the day.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jaxson Dart clears concussion protocol After exiting the field and undergoing a concussion test, Giants rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart was cleared and returned to the field midway through the third quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, the Giants announced that Dart is dealing with a hamstring issue, which is evident by his stretching and limping.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jaxson Dart out of the game Following a collision on a long run that was called back due to a John Michael Schmitz penalty, quarterback Jaxson Dart was forced to exit the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: An independent doctor called down for Dart to be examined for a possible concussion.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dart has also been dealing with a clear hamstring issue.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nabers believed to have suffered torn ACL In the worst possible news, but what seemed to be expected, Nabers is believed to have suffered a torn ACL.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Deonte Banks burned With just seconds remaining in the second quarter, Giants cornerback Deonte Banks did the one thing he couldn't afford to do: Get beat off the snap and surrender a 36-yard touchdown to Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Quarterback Justin Herbert threw a good ball, dropping it in front of the safety, but the space was created by Banks biting on a juke.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 13, Chargers 10 at halftime.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Another redzone stall After driving 47 yards on 15 plays, the Giants' offense, sans wide receiver Malik Nabers, stalled in the redzone once again.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Constant pressure and the absence of a top receiving target doomed them.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants ultimately settled for a 31-yard Jude McAtamney field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 13, Chargers 3 Jaxson Dart limping Rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart appears to be dealing with a hamstring issue.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He's been seen stretching his left leg and with roughly 2:00 remaining in the first half, is now limping.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Malik Nabers injured Midway through the second quarter, quarterback Jaxson Dart launched a deep pass down the sideline to wide receiver Malik Nabers, who appeared to have injured his right knee as he went up for the ball.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He remained on the ground, clutching his knee as trainers rushed onto the field.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The cart was ultimately brought out for Nabers, who was then driven into the locker room.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Safety Jevon Holland was also revealed to have sustained a neck injury.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He is questionable to return.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Chargers on the board Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, under constant pressure, inched the offense down the field, going 40 yards over 10 plays.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: An Abdul Carter would-be sack led to an intentional grounding and a fourth down, leaving Los Angeles to settle for a Cameron Dicker 47-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 10, Chargers 3 Redzone woes continue After Dexter Lawrence returned an interception inside the 5-yard line, the Giants' offense, with rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart under center, still couldn't get anything done.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They went three-and-out with minus-one net yards, settling for a 22-yard Jude McAtamney field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 10, Chargers 0 Sexy Dexy INT Nose tackle Dexter Lawrence, who has dominated throughout the first quarter, got his hands up in the lane during a double-team and tipped it back to himself for an interception.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He ran it back to the four-yard line before finally being stopped.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was the second pass defensed for Lawrence in the game and his first career interception.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Defense holds Despite two unnecessary penalties and some undisciplined play on a third-and-18, the Giants managed to hold the Chargers offense and force a punt, which was downed at the 1-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dart is back under center for his second NFL drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jaxson Dart touchdown Rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart capped his first-ever NFL drive in style, weaving his way to the endzone with a 15-yard score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The drive went 89 yards over nine plays and ate up 4:17 (largely no-huddle).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants 7, Chargers 0 Jaxson Dart first NFL completion After the defense forced a three-and-out (aided by a Chargers penalty and drop), rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart took the field to a defeaning ovation.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dart's first play was a handoff to rookie running back Cam Skattebo for five yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The next play, he targeted wide receiver Malik Nabers, who drew a defensive pass interference.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two plays later, Dart completed his first NFL pass to Nabers for seven yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants win toss, defer The Giants won the coin toss and opted to defer.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Chargers will start with the football, and New York will receive the second-half kickoff.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The debut of rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart will have to wait just a bit more.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Big ovation for Jaxson Dart The Giants introduced the offense before kickoff, and rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart, who was sent out first, received a big ovation from the crowd.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: No protests Entering the weekend, fans had planned for and paid for three plane protests.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, with a noon hour coming and going, none flew over MetLife Stadium.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A change at quarterback may have staved off the banners...

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: For now.

text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys dominate Jets, 37-22 Oct 05, 2025 at 03:26 PM Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Desperately needing a win, many wondered just how this Dallas Cowboys team could in fact earn a victory with so many injuries hitting the starting lineup.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fortunately, though, they were playing the New York Jets.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Behind an explosive offense and a defense that had its best performance of the young season, the Cowboys dominated their hosts, 37-22.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Still, although New York was winless coming into the matchup, this wasn't going to be an easy affair for Dallas.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Or at least that was the original thought, considering that four of the Cowboys' five starting offensive linemen were out injured.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith did suit up in case of an emergency, but he spent the day resting on the sideline.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, with Dak Prescott continuing his masterful play, there was seemingly no hiccup in the Dallas offense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The quarterback completed 18 of 29 passes for 237 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions for a 127.4 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Benefiting from Prescott's impressive play was second-year man Ryan Flournoy, who had more receiving yards in this game (114) than he did in all of his 2024 rookie season (102).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Also heavily involved in the passing attack was a familiar face, Jake Ferguson.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The tight end had seven catches for 49 receiving yards but also registered two scoring grabs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And Javonte Williams continued his successful campaign on the ground, finishing with 135 rushing yards, which marked his first time cracking the century mark in a Dallas uniform.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In addition, he had a touchdown as well.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But an even bigger surprise than the offense overcoming its injuries was perhaps the play of the Dallas defense as Jets quarterback Justin Fields was sacked five times.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He did throw for 283 yards and two touchdowns, but most of that came in garbage time with the game already decided.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Breece Hall's 113 rushing yards fueled a New York running game that went for 144 yards, but it wasn't nearly enough.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rookie linebacker Shemar James led the Cowboys with 15 tackles while James Houston was one of five players to record at least a half-sack, earning 1½. Overall, in a penalty-fille game that saw a total of 21 flags thrown, the Cowboys outgained the Jets, 416 to 378, converted 46 percent of their third downs and were 3 of 4 in the red zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter The Jets put together a lengthy drive to open the game, using 13 plays and over seven minutes of clock time to travel 66 yards to the Dallas 3-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But there the Cowboys' defense stood strong, limiting the damage to a 25-yard field goal with New York going on top early, 3-0.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It would be the Jets' first and last lead of the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Forty of the Cowboys' 49 yards gained during their first possession came on a deep pass to Flournoy down the right sideline, but the team had to settle for a field goal of its own.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Brandon Aubrey, the NFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September, continued his hot streak, getting the three points from 35 yards out to even the score after one quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter The Cowboys then opened the second frame with a first-and-10 at the Jets' 47-yard line after Prescott beat the blitz with a quick slant to George Pickens for 14 yards, which in turn led to Dallas eventually getting its first touchdown of the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: To cap the 13-play, 90-yard drive, Ferguson hauled in a short pass and then raced to the goal line for the 26-yard score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Late in the quarter, New York was knocking on the door again, holding a first-and-10 at the Cowboys' 23-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But on the tail end of a 10-yard gain by Hall, Dallas linebacker Marist Liufau punched the ball out and teammate Sam Wiliams fell on the fumble to end the threat.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That gave Prescott and company just over two minutes to work with; they needed only 1:21.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite a penalty backing the Cowboys up to their own 5-yard line, the quarterback made quick work of the Jets defense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He found Flournoy for gains of 10 and 46 yards with a 14-yard scramble himself in between.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Williams took care of the rest.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He first went around the left end for an 11-yard gain and then came right back and went 5 yards around the right end for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But the Cowboys weren't done yet.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the defense forced a quick three-and-out, Dallas got the ball back at its own 33-yard line with 29 seconds left.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And that's when Williams broke through the line off left guard, bolted into the open field and scampered 66 yards before being knocked out of bounds at the 1-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott then connected with Ferguson again, the pair combing for their second touchdown of the day.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And while Aubrey saw his extra-point attempt doink off the right upright, the Cowboys still went into the break with a comfortable 23-3 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third quarter Although the Cowboys offense couldn't keep the momentum going early in the second half, the team's defense made sure the New Yorkers didn't do much either.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And when the unit stopped the Jets on fourth-and-1 at the Dallas 47-yard line, Prescott and his troops were set up with good field position to begin their next drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After Flournoy went around the left end for 10 yards on first snap of the series, Prescott went for it all on the next one.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He threw deep to Pickens, who corralled the ball in the end zone for a big 43-yard touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The rout was officially on, 30-3.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Jets did manage to add three points to their scoreboard total before the end of the quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A six-play, 44-yard drive finished with a 48-yard field goal by Nick Folk, snapping the Cowboys' streak of 30 unanswered points.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter With the outcome essentially decided, there was nothing really left to do but play out the clock.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Jets did finally get into the end zone, thanks to a 10-play, 78-yard drive that first saw Fields complete a 16-yard pass to Hall on fourth-and-5 at the Dallas 17.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The New York quarterback then connected with fullback Andrew Beck for the touchdown and followed that up with a pass to tight end Mason Taylor for the two-point conversion, the score now 30-14.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But when Jalen Tolbert recovered the Jets' onside-kick attempt, the Cowboys again had good field possession to begin a drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And they took advantage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A short pass to Williams got Dallas back on the board and marked the 12 th game in his career that Prescott has thrown at least four touchdown passes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Jets did add one more touchdown, although it was of course too little too late.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A 9-yard pass from Fields to Garrett Wilson got New York in the end zone, and after picking up the two-point conversion, the day's scoring was done, 37-22.

text: Home / NFL NFL AFC contender swings massive trade deadline blockbuster In a massive move ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are acquiring cornerback Sauce Gardner from the New York Jets.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Alex Barth Updated Nov 5, 2025 12:29 PM EST EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – OCTOBER 05:

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Sauce Gardner #1 of the New York Jets takes the field prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on October 05, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Sarah Stier/Getty Images Share this story Entering the NFL trade deadline the New England Patriots, Indianapolis Colts, and Denver Broncos are all tied for the best record in the AFC.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline the Colts became the first team from that group to strike, acquiring cornerback Sauce Gardner from the New York Jets.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The trade, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , has the Colts acquiring Gardner in exchange for two first-round picks.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Those picks are the Colts' own picks for the next two drafts - 2026 and 2027.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: New York also gets second-year wide receiver AD Mitchell , who was the 52nd overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This move comes as the Colts have been one of the biggest surprises in the NFL this season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Led by a resurging Daniel Jones , Indy stood alone with the best record in the league before losing to the Steelers on Sunday.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Colts lead the league averaging 32.2 points per game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Defensively the Colts are still a top 10 unit allowing 20.1 points per game, but their pass defense has been inconsistent.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That unit ranks 26th in the NFL in yards allowed, and 11th in net yards per pass attempt allowed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They now add a two-time all-pro in Gardner, who was drafted by the Jets fourth overall in the 2022 NFL Draft.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 25-year-old had just signed a four-year, $120.4 million contract extension with the Jets this past offseason.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Moving on from Gardner highlights the fact that the Jets are likely looking at another rebuild ahead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: New York is 1-7 under first-year head coach Aaron Glenn , and even with Gardner has the 27th-ranked defense through nine weeks.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This takes Gardner off of the Patriots' upcoming schedule not once, but twice.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Patriots haven't played the Jets yet this season, with those matchups slated for a Thursday Night Football matchup next week in Foxborough, and then a meeting in New Jersey in Week 17.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, the Patriots could end up seeing Gardner and the Colts in the postseason if both sides keep up their level of play from the first half of the year.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Will the Patriots also make a move to keep pace with the Colts in the AFC?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They - and the rest of the league - have until 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday to get any deals done.
