text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys lose to Carolina, 30-27 Oct 12, 2025 at 03:24 PM Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When you have the No. 1 offense and a last-place defense, every game can be a rollercoaster ride.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And though Dak Prescott and his troops had put the Dallas Cowboys in the win column in previous outings, this time they couldn't make up for a leaky defensive unit as the Carolina Panthers pulled out the victory, 30-27.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Panthers running back Rico Dowdle had warned his former Cowboys teammates that they had better "buckle up."

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He wasn't lying.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After running for 206 yards last weekend, he picked up right where he left off against a Dallas defense that struggled to stop both Carolina's ground and aerial attacks.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dowdle finished the game with 186 rushing yards on 30 tries, a 6.1 yards per carry average.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In doing so, he became the first former Cowboy to rush for more than 100 yards against his former team.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Not that the Dallas defense did much better against the Carolina passing game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Bryce Young threw for 199 yards with three touchdowns and an interception for a 114.8 rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dowdle added to that effort with another 56 receiving yards for his second straight game with more than 200 yards from scrimmage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Meanwhile, Prescott and his side of the ball tried to do their part.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The star quarterback completed 73.5 percent of his passes for 261 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions for a 124.8 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He and George Pickens were simply on a different level than everyone else, as they connected nine times for 168 yards and a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And Prescott had to do the heavy lifting for the offense because the rushing effort was anemic.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Javaonte Williams managed only 29 yards on 13 carries while the group as a whole averaged just 1.6 yards per attempt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overall, the Cowboys were outgained 410 to 292 and came up short in the time of possession, 32:02 to 27:58.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter After the Cowboys went a quick three-and-out, the team was perhaps fortunate to be down only 3-0 once Carolina was done with its opening turn.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Behind Dowdle's 42 yards from scrimmage and a 21-yard pass to tight end Mitchell Evans, the Panthers got down to Dallas' 13-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But there the defense stood its ground, forcing the home side to settle for a 31-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, it didn't take long for Prescott and the offense to get going as the Cowboys tied the game with a 10-play, 68-yard drive.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The highlight moment came when Pickens grabbed a Prescott pass, hurdled a Carolina defender and raced down the left sideline to the Panthers' 8 for a 31-yard gain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite having first-and-goal, though, Dallas also was forced to kick a field goal, the 23-yarder evening things up, 3-3.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And thanks to the defense, the Cowboys soon had the ball back.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Late in the first quarter, Carolina had a first-and-10 at its own 41, but Young's pass went off the hands of his target, Tetairoa McMillan, and into the diving arms of Donovan Wilson.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The safety then got up and ran the ball down to the Panthers' 12-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter The drive wrapped up on the Cowboys' first snap of the second frame.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With Dallas facing a fourth-and-1 at the 3-yard line, Prescott found Hunter Luepke wide open on the left side of the end zone for the game's first touchdown and the first scoring catch of the fullback's career.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Regardless, Dowdle was proving to be a tough customer as he picked up 31 more rushing yards on Carolina's next series.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But it was a 19-yard pass to McMillan that got the Panthers across the goal line, again tying the score, 10-10.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: No matter, Prescott was really heating up now.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He completed 8 of 9 passes for 68 yards on the Cowboys' next possession, the last of which was a 19-yard completion to tight end Jake Ferguson for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Perhaps more impressive, on fourth-and-4 at the Panthers' 30-yard line, head coach Brian Schottenheimer elected to go for it instead of turning to trusted kicker Brandon Aubrey.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The decision paid off with an 8-yard pass from Prescott to Pickens and the eventual score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Carolina was able to add three more points before the half with a 55-yard field goal, but the Cowboys still went into the break with a 17-13 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter This seesaw affair wasn't anywhere close to being done, though.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Miscommunication again seemed to plague the Dallas secondary as on the first play of the third quarter, Carolina wideout Jimmy Horn was left wide open for a 34-yard gain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The four-play, 80-yard drive then came to an end when Dowdle got behind the defense on a wheel route for a 36-yard touchdown pass.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: So now it was Prescott's turn.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He led his men on a six-play, 73-yard series that saw him complete 4 of 5 passes, three of which were thrown to Pickens.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That included the touchdown toss when the quarterback found his target streaking across the middle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Pickens then turned on the jets and darted through the Carolina defense to pay dirt, Dallas back on top 24-20.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter Despite the offense's continued success, at this point the Dallas defense seemingly had no solutions for stopping the Panthers when they had the ball.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: As the clock ticked over into the fourth quarter, Dowdle continued to pound away at their forces, rushing five times for 37 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The scoring honors, though, would go to McMillan, who got his second touchdown to provide Carolina with another lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Who would blink first?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys nearly did, but on a third-and-5 at his own 35-yard line, Prescott again connected with Pickens, who spun away from the defense for a 45-yard gain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas went on to get to the Panthers' 8

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: but that would be it, and Aubrey had to come out for a 28-yard field goal to tie the game, 27-27.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When the Cowboys defense then finally – finally!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: – got a three-and-out stop, it seemed that would be the break the team needed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But unable to take advantage, the Dallas offense then had to punt for only the third time all game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Meaning, the defense desperately needed another stop.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They couldn't get it.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It looked like the Cowboys actually did when a Carolina pass on third-and-7 at its own 17-yard line fell incomplete, but a pass interference penalty on Kaiir Elam moved the chains and the possession continued.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And later in the series, another Young attempt was no good on third-and-4 at the Dallas 40-yard line, but the Panthers converted the fourth down try to keep the drive alive as the clock hit the two-minute warning.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When Carolina then picked up a first down at the Dallas 12-yard line with 1:01 remaining, and the Cowboys out of timeouts, Young simply kneeled the ball twice to run the time down to three seconds.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Ryan Fitzgerald then kicked the 33-yard field goal as the clock hit zeroes to capture the 30-27 win.

text: Drummond Cowboys Wire Updated Oct. 12, 2025, 3:24 p.m. CT

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Dallas Cowboys had made their way back into the win column in Week 5, and were looking to establish a winning streak as they approach the midpoint of their season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas hasdn't lost since Week 3 and were looking to extend their undefeated streak to three as they took on the Panthers in Carolina's Bank of America Stadium.

subject: Dallas Cowboys

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: By John Breech Oct 13, 2025 at 12:57 pm ET • 18 min read Getty Images Welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: I'd like to start things off here by wishing a happy birthday to Jerry Jones.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He's turning 83 today and if his birthday wish was for the Cowboys to win in Week 6, then that's unfortunate, because his team lost to the Panthers .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And to add insult to injury, the Panthers best player in the game ( Rico Dowdle ) was a player who the Cowboys could have re-signed during the offseason, but they decided to let him walk in free agency.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And based on that decision alone, maybe Jerry's birthday wish should be for his team to get a new general manager.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The loss by the Cowboys was so embarrassing that the always talkative Jones didn't even want to talk with the media after the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fortunately, I'm in the mood to talk right now and I've got a lot to say, so let's get to the rundown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: As always, here's your reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: To get them signed up, all you have to do is click here .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: 1. NFL Week 6 grades: Bengals earn 'C+' in Joe Flacco's first game Getty Images Welcome to my favorite part of the Monday newsletter, which is where I hand out grades for all 32 teams.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Actually, this week, I didn't grade all 32 teams because there were two teams on a bye, and then we have four teams playing tonight, so you're only getting 26 grades.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Anyway, here are the grades from three notable games that were played Sunday:

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Broncos 13-11 over Jets in London ( full recap )

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Broncos takeaway: We don't hand out an offensive grade and a defensive grade, but for the Broncos, we should probably do that for this game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The defense gets an "A+" for a dominant performance that saw the Broncos rack up nine sacks.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Denver gave Nik Bonitto a $120 million contract at the beginning of the season and he's already looking like a bargain.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Broncos held the Jets to -10 passing yards, which was the lowest total the NFL has seen in 27 years.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Patrick Surtain II absolutely shut down Garrett Wilson , who had just 13 yards receiving.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Offensively, the Broncos struggled for the second straight week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If the offense can get things figured out, the Broncos could quickly turn into the favorite in the AFC West.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Even with the offense struggling, the Broncos are definitely a Super Bowl contender with this defense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Grade: C+ Jets takeaway: The Jets defense played well enough to win.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Jets special teams played well enough to win, but the offense apparently didn't make the trip to England.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The offense seems to be getting worse every week and it hit rock bottom in London in a game where New York had NEGATIVE passing yards ( Justin Fields threw for 45 yards, but the team lost 55 yards on nine sacks for a total of -10 passing yards).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If the Jets learned one thing from this game, it's that Fields simply isn't the answer at quarterback.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The ugly offensive day overshadowed a defense that held the Broncos to just 71 yards in the second half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Jets are 0-6 and going nowhere.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Grade: C- Packers 27-18 over Bengals ( full recap )

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Bengals takeaway: Joe Flacco only had four days to learn the Bengals' offense, and during the first half, he played like a guy who only had four days to learn the offense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, the Bengals should be encouraged by the fact that something seemed to click for Flacco during a second half in which he completed 70% of his passes for 179 yards and two touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Flacco spread the ball around: He completed at least one pass to eight different receivers, including Ja'Marr Chase , who had 10 receptions for 94 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite the loss, the Bengals will likely now have plenty of confidence going into their showdown with the Steelers on Thursday night.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Grade: C+ Packers takeaway: This was a surprisingly close game going into the fourth quarter with Green Bay leading just 10-7, and that's when Jordan Love took over.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Packers piled up 17 points in the quarter thanks to 74 passing yards and a touchdown from Love.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With the Packers unable to shake the feisty Bengals, Green Bay needed everything Love had to offer.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Packers offense also got a spark from Josh Jacobs , who scored two touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: There are still some major question marks about Green Bay's once dominant defense -- a defense that couldn't stop Joe Flacco in the second half -- but those questions are much easier to ask when your team is winning like the Packers did on Sunday.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Grade: B- Chiefs 30-17 over Lions ( full recap ) Lions takeaway: The Lions had the longest winning streak in the NFL heading into Week 6, but it came to an abrupt end in Kansas City.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Lions offense generally struggles when it can't run the ball and the Lions couldn't the run the ball during a second half where they were limited to just six yards on the ground.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Defensively, the Lions went into this game with a banged up secondary

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: and it certainly showed as they got diced up by Patrick Mahomes .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When the Lions are healthy, they're one of the best teams in the NFL, but if they don't get healthy soon, it's going to be tough for them to stop any team with a good quarterback.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And that's bad news for a Lions team that will be hosting Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers next week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Grade: C- Chiefs takeaway: The Chiefs looked beatable through the first few weeks of the season, but they made a statement on Sunday night and that statement is that they're still one of the best teams in the NFL.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This a dominant performance, especially by a Chiefs offense that only punted once in the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Patrick Mahomes had his way with the Lions defense, totaling 289 yards and four touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Travis Kelce had his biggest game of the season for a Chiefs offense that has now scored at least 28 points in four straight games for the first time in three years.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The biggest surprise here was the way the Chiefs' defense manhandled the Lions, holding them to just 112 yards in the second half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Chiefs will now be getting Rashee Rice back in Week 7 and a team that some left for dead after their 0-2 start once again feels like one of the favorites in the AFC.

text: 2. NFL Week 6 winners and losers: Backup running backs rule the week You can't have a week of NFL action without having winners and losers, so we have some winners and losers.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jared Dubin came up with this week's list, and we're going to check out his winners, which featured two running backs who were thrust into the starting job this month.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: WINNERS Panthers RB Rico Dowdle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dowdle talked some pregame smack to his former team, telling the Dallas Cowboys that they should buckle up their chin straps to get ready to play against him and the Carolina Panthers.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: (Dallas allowed Dowdle to walk in free agency this offseason, choosing instead to sign Javonte Williams and Miles Sanders .)

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dowdle came out against Dallas and backed up his talk with his play: he went over 200 total yards for the second week in a row, rushing an incredible 30 times for 183 yards and catching four passes for 56 yards and a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Chargers' second-year running back had a breakout game in L.A.'s first week without either Omarion Hampton or Najee Harris .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Vidal went for 124 yards on 18 carries, while also catching three passes for 14 yards and a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Initially expected to work behind the veteran Hassan Haskins , Vidal was instead the lead back for the Chargers and played a key role in their win over the Dolphins .

text: 4. Crazy stats from Week 6: Jets offense crashes in London Every Sunday night, I get an email from our research department here at CBS Sports, and every Sunday, that email always includes some wild stats about the games that were just played.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that in mind, here are 13 crazy stats from Week 6: Jets' passing game crashes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Jets finished with NEGATIVE 10 passing yards, which was the lowest total that the NFL has seen in 27 years.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The last team to go lower came in 1998 when Ryan Leaf and the Chargers totaled -19 passing yards in a game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If you're wondering how the Jets hit their total, Justin Field threw for 45 yards, but lost 55 yards on nine sacks and that 55-yard loss is added to their team passing total.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Broncos beat up on the Jets.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Broncos lead the NFL with 30 sacks on the season and nine of those game on Sunday against the Jets.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Broncos have now tallied at least five sacks in four of their first six games, making them just the third team since 1990 to pull off that feat (They joined the 2000 Buccaneers and 2019 Patriots ).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: McCaffrey is carrying the 49ers .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Christian McCaffrey finished with 57 yards receiving during the 49ers' 30-19 loss to the Buccaneers.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That makes him the first running back in NFL history with at least 50 yards receiving in each of his team's first six games of the season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Titans are still bad.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Titans are the only team in the NFL that still hasn't held a fourth-quarter lead this season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Titans do have one win, but that came on a field goal as time expired.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rico's revenge:

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Panthers running back Rico Dowdle had 239 total yards against the Cowboys on Sunday after totaling 234 last week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That makes Dowdle just the seventh player in NFL history to total at least 230 scrimmage yards in back-to-back games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dowdle accomplished the feat this week against a Cowboys team that decided not to keep him for 2025 after he spent his first four seasons with the team.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Cowboys collapse.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys became the 79th team since 1970 to average 30 points per game with zero turnovers over a three-game span.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The other 78 teams finished with a winning record during that span, but the Cowboys didn't, going 1-1-1.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Browns can't win in Pittsburgh.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With their 23-9 loss to the Steelers, the Browns have now lost 22 straight games in Pittsburgh, which is the second-longest losing streak by any team in one city in NFL history.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The only longer streak came when the Lions lost 23 straight in Green Bay from 1992 through 2014.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Baker's dozen.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Over the past two weeks, Baker Mayfield has thrown for 635 yards while throwing just 10 incompletions.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It's the most passing yards (635) on 10 or fewer incompletions in a two-game span since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Joe Flacco joins rare club.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 40-year-old became just the seventh QB in NFL history to face the same opponent twice in one season, but with a different team each time.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Back in Week 3, Flacco beat the Packers while playing for the Browns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On Sunday, he threw two touchdowns in a 27-18 loss to Green Bay while playing for the Bengals.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Indiana Jones and Colts crusade.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Colts have scored 194 points through six weeks, which is notable, because that's the most they've scored through six games since 1964 when they scored 203.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That means that the Colts are scoring points at a higher point with Daniel Jones than they did during any season with Peyton Manning .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Packers shutout streak continues.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With the Bengals scoring zero points in the first quarter, the Packers still haven't given up a single first-quarter point this year.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Their five-game streak is the longest stretch to start a season since 2015 when the Broncos held their first seven opponents scoreless in the first quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Broncos ended up winning that Super Bowl that year.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Ja'Marr Chase goes off.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Bengals receiver caught 10 passes for 94 yards and a touchdown, marking the 12th time in his career that he's caught at least 10 passes with at least one TD.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That's the fourth-most by any receiver in NFL history, trailing only Davante Adams (18), Antonio Brown (14) and Tyreek Hill (13).

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: All three of those players took at least 145 games to accomplish the feat.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: For Chase, it took just 68.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The 67-yard field goal that didn't count.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Bengals kicker Evan McPherson appeared to set an NFL record on Sunday with a 67-yard field goal against the Packers, but the kick didn't count, because Matt LaFleur called a timeout just before the play started.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: McPherson ended up missing his second attempt after the timeout.

text: If you want to see the 67-yard kick that went in, be sure to check it out here .

text: If you see any other fun facts, feel free to tweet them at me .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Monday night doubleheader is back: We've got two games tonight For the third time this season, we're getting a Monday night doubleheader, which means we'll be getting two games tonight.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The NFL schedule included a total of four Monday night doubleheaders this year.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This is the third one and the final one will be coming next week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The first game of the night will feature Buffalo (4-1) at Atlanta (2-2) in a game that will kick off at 7:15 p.m. ET on ESPN.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Here's one reason why each team should be feeling confident going into the game: Why the Bills can win: Over the past three weeks, the Falcons defense has faced J.J. McCarthy , Bryce Young and Marcus Mariota , so Josh Allen will be a huge challenge compared to those three.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If the Falcons focus on stopping Allen, that should give James Cook a chance to take over.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Falcons are surrendering 4.6 yards per carry this year, which means there should be a lot of holes for Cook to run through.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Since the start of the 2024 season, the Bills are 7-0 when he rushes for at least 100 yards, so If Cook goes off, it's hard to see the Bills losing.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Why the Falcons can win: The Falcons need to get Bijan Robinson involved early and often and that's mostly because they'll be facing a Bills defense that's surrendering 145.6 yards per game on the ground this year, which is the third-worst in the NFL.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If Robinson is running the ball well, that will keep the Falcons offense on the field and Josh Allen off of it.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Falcons are 2-0 this year when Robinson tops 125 scrimmage yards and 0-2 when he doesn't.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: You can get a full preview of the game from Jared Dubin by clicking here .

text: In the late game, we've got the Bears (2-2) hosting the Commanders (3-2) at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Here's one reason why each of these teams could pull out the win: Why the Bears can win: If there's one way to attack the Commanders defense, it's through the air, which means there's going to be a lot of pressure on Caleb Williams to come up with a big performance tonight.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Williams has improved every week while running Ben Johnson's offense and this will be a chance for him to prove on a national stage just how far he's come along.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If Williams plays smart football and doesn't turn the ball over, that should put the Bears in a position to win the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Why the Commanders can win: The Commanders have the top rushing offense in the NFL and they get to face a Bears team that has surrendered the second-most rushing yards per game through five weeks.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With receivers Terry McLaurin and Noah Brown both out tonight and Deebo Samuel coming off a week where he was limited in practice, look for the Commanders to try and establish the run early.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Since the start of the 2024 season, the Commanders are 11-0 when they rush for 150 yards or more, so if they can hit that magic number, they'll likely walk away with the win.

text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys in command, 44-22 Oct 19, 2025 at 06:49 PM

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: While the Cowboys offense did what they've been doing all season, scoring plenty of points, Matt Eberflus' much-maligned defensive unit finally took a step forward in the team's 44-22 victory over the rival Washington Commanders.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Was it a dominating performance?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Perhaps not, but with more blitzing and man coverage as well as a season-high in takeaways, Dallas largely kept in check a Commanders offense that came into the game ranked seventh in points scored and 13 th in total yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Before leaving in the third quarter due to a hamstring injury, Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels completed just 54.5 percent of his passes for 156 yards with a touchdown and a fumble for a 92.2 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Commanders' ground game found success with 136 rushing yards for a 4.9 yards per carry average, although 69 of those yards were provided by quarterbacks Daniels and Marcus Mariota.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, when the offense is putting up forty points that certainly makes life easier.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dak Prescott continued his MVP-caliber season, completing 70 percent of his throws for 264 yards and three touchdowns for a 130.4 rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: As expected, or at least hoped, wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens indeed proved to be a dynamic duo.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Lamb, who hadn't played in a game since Week 3 due to injury, averaged 22.0 yards per catch, finishing with 110 yards and a touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Meanwhile, Pickens averaged 20.5 himself for a total of 82 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Just for good measure, tight end Jake Ferguson hauled in a game-high seven catches, which included two touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And running back Javontae Williams shouldn't be forgotten.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Following a tough outing last week, he rebounded in this one with a season-high 116 rushing yards and a touchdown, averaging 6.1 yards per carry.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In all, the Cowboys outgained Washington, 409 to 341, converted 75 percent of their opportunities in the red zone and held the time of possession, 31:21 to 28:39.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter After winning the opening coin toss, the Cowboys chose to take the ball and get the game going with their offense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Good call, as KaVontae Turpin, returning from injury as well, brought the kickoff back 30 yards to the Dallas 34.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Lamb then got into the swing of things with a 13-yard catch on third-and-1.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The big blow, though, came when Pickens caused a Washington pass interference penalty on a deep 37-yard throw, which set Dallas up at the Commanders' 2-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Williams then powered across the goal line for an early 7-0 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys had a chance to then really put their foot on the gas when the defense forced a quick three-and-out.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But following a 58-yard Commanders punt that pinned Dallas at its own 1-yard line, Washington defense tackle Daron Payne manhandled his way into the backfield to take down Williams for a safety.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And upon getting the ball right back, the visitors wasted no time in getting their first touchdown of the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Going no-huddle, Daniels hit Chris Moore for a 44-yard gain, which led to a sharp pass to tight end Zach Ertz for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Cowboys cornerback Daron Bland brought down Daniels to stop the two-point conversion try, but Washington still had the lead, 8-7.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: No matter, Prescott and company were already firing on all cylinders.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys responded with a 47-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey, and then after the defense forced another punt, Lamb hauled in a deep pass down the middle before speeding away from the Washington secondary for a 74-yard touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, Dallas was on top for good, 17-8.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter Though the sledding got a little tougher for the offense, the Cowboys are seemingly never far from field-goal range.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And sure enough, despite stalling at the Washington 43 on their second possession of the quarter, Aubrey came out and split the uprights on a 61-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In doing so, he set the NFL record for the most career field goals of at least 60 yards with five.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Up to this point, the Dallas defense had forced four punts and stopped Washington on a fourth-down attempt, but with just under two minutes left in the half, the Cowboys couldn't get off the field.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Daniels would push his way into the end zone from the 1-yard line for the touchdown as the Commanders pulled to within 20-15.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, the 39 seconds remaining on the clock was plenty of time for Dallas to reach pay dirt themselves.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite Prescott being sacked on the first play of the series, he bounced back with a 44-yard pass to Pickens, which was followed by a 33-yard rush by Williams to the Washington 2.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A strike from Prescott to Ferguson then provided the score, Dallas going into the break with a 27-15 advantage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter The Cowboys defense found its rhythm again as the second half got underway.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Commanders had reached the Dallas 39-yard line, but blitzing linebacker Shemar James jarred the ball loose from Daniels, who would then leave injured, and defensive end Jadeveon Clowney fell on the fumble to end the threat.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Given the gift, Wiliams got the next drive rolling with a pair of runs for a combined 25 yards with Prescott then completing four of five passes for 22 yards, plus a 7-yard scramble.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The last of those throw was a 5-yard completion to Ferguson for his second touchdown of the day.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When Mariota, under intense pressure, then threw an ill-advised pass to Jeremy McNichols on the right sideline, it was ball game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That's because Bland cut in front of the would-be receiver, intercepted the throw and raced untouched 68 yards for the pick-6 touchdown, the Cowboys now owning a commanding 41-15 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, the Commanders weren't ready to fade into the setting sun just yet.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Helped by a questionable pass interference call on Kaiir Elam on fourth-and-8 at the Dallas 26-yard line, Washington capped off a 7-play, 53-yard drive with a 3-yard dive across the goal line by Chris Rodriguez.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter As the final frame got under way, the Cowboys found themselves with a first down at the Commanders' 15-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And while they couldn't reach the end zone, Aubrey came out for a chip-shot 29-yard field goal to double-up the score, 44-22.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And with that, there was nothing left to do but play out the clock, the Cowboys moving into second place in the tight NFC East with a 3-3-1 record.

text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys in Denver, 44-24 Oct 26, 2025 at 06:50 PM Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When the Dallas Cowboys missed a golden opportunity to get into the end zone in the early minutes of their game at the Denver Broncos, the tone of the day was seemingly set.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Field goals weren't going to win this one.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: As proven by the Broncos, who would quickly take a lead they would never relinquish, going on to hand the Cowboys a 44-24 drubbing.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The loss extended Dallas' losing streak against the Broncos to eight games with the Cowboys having not won a matchup in Denver since the 1992 season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This one was supposed to feature strength vs. strength with Dallas' top offense going up against the Broncos' formidable defense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Unfortunately, it was the Denver side that held the upper hand throughout most of the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Under pressure all afternoon, Dak Prescott threw for just 188 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, his first picks since Week 3 at Chicago.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That led to a disappointing 51.5 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both had seven catches for 74 and 78 yards, respectively, but tight end Jake Ferguson, who came into the game ranked fourth in the NFL with 51 receptions, was held without a catch.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Not that things were a whole lot better on the ground.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Running back Javonte Williams scored twice, but totaled only 41 yards rushing on 13 carries, the Cowboys as a group averaging 3.5 yards per attempt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, it may have taken an otherworldly effort on the offense's part anyway because the Dallas defense could do little to slow down the Broncos' offensive attack.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Denver quarterback Bo Nix exploited a Cowboys secondary that was riddled with injuries and was simply in over its collective heads.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He threw for 247 yards with four touchdowns and an interception for a 117.4 rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins topped 100 yards rushing, totaling 111, but it was rookie R.J. Harvey who had a career day.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He ran for just 46 yards but scored twice on the ground and also had a touchdown catch.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overall, the Cowboys totaled 339 yards of offense while converting 36 percent of their third down tries and 50 percent of their red-zone opportunities.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But on the other side of the ball, the Broncos picked up 426 yards with a 63 percent conversion rate on third downs and an 80 percent mark in the red zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter The Cowboys got off to a good start, but not a great one.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Denver chose to take the ball first, but three plays into the game, it was Dallas rookie cornerback Trikweze Bridges taking the ball away from the Broncos with his first career interception.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Starting at their own 48-yard line, the Cowboys offense worked its way down to the Denver 1, but after failing to get into the end zone, Brandon Aubrey came out for a chip-shot 24-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And that missed opportunity for an early touchdown soon came back to bite the Cowboys as the Broncos promptly scored touchdowns on their next two possessions to jump out to a 14-3 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The first needed only five plays to go 74 yards to the goal line with Harvey scampering untouched 40 yards for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After a Dallas punt, Denver then used just four plays to cover 62 yards for a second touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nix completed passes of 16, 10 and then 25 during the drive, the last of which was a scoring toss to slot receiver Troy Franklin.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter Thankfully, the Dallas offense found a little rhythm in the second frame.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rookie running back Jaydon Blue got things started with a 14-yard run, although it was a 14-yard pass from Prescott to tight end Luke Schoonmaker later in the series that set the Cowboys up with a first-and-goal at the Denver 1.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Williams then got the scoring honors, bulldozing up the middle to close the gap to 14-10.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, the Broncos responded with 13 more points before the end of the half to essentially put the game away.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The big blow on their next possession came via a 32-yard pass interference penalty on rookie safety Alijah Clark, which was followed by an 11-yard catch and run by tight end Evan Engram.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Now with a first-and-goal, Harvey took a direct snap back up the middle for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With an unnecessary roughness penalty on Dallas defensive end Sam Williams after the play, the Broncos decided to go for the two-point conversion, but the Cowboys managed to foil the attempt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Desperately needing to get some more points on the board, Prescott and company instead went a quick three-and-out, which gave Denver plenty of time to increase its lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With Nix completing all six of his passes, the Broncos marched 72 yards in seven plays and only 1:35 off the clock to score again.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The touchdown came when Nix connected with wideout Pat Bryant in the back left corner of the end zone, giving Denver a 27-10 advantage at the break.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter Fortunately, the Dallas offense found its spark again as the second half got underway as the team traveled 65 yards in 13 plays to pay dirt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott was clutch throughout, scrambling 9 yards on third-and-3 at the Cowboys' 42-yard line for a first down before later finding Pickens on fourth-and-3 at the Denver 27-yard line, the receiver making an outstanding tiptoe catch for 17 yards to move the chains.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Helped by a pair of pass interference penalties inside the 10, Dallas got its needed touchdown when Williams drove up the middle for his second score of the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: At this point, though, the Cowboys defense was showing little signs of slowing down the Broncos.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The fact the unit held Denver to a 42-yard field goal on its next series was perhaps a small victory of sorts.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Regardless, Dallas was now down 30-17.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter Last week, the Broncos had an unlikely 33-point fourth quarter to pull off a come-from-behind victory over the New York Giants.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys, though, would not capture that same magic in this one, especially with Dallas now having to employ a cornerback at safety due to a rib injury to Clark.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After the Cowboys made the decision to punt on fourth-and-6 at their own 44-yard line, the Broncos came right back with a 12-play, 84-yard drive for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Nix picked apart the ragtag secondary, his final 7-yard throw going to a wide-open Franklin in the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: While the outcome was already decided, Prescott tried his best to make the scoreboard at least look respectable.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But on first-and-10 at the Denver 11-yard line, he and Lamb weren't on the same page, leading to an interception by linebacker Dondrea Tillman, who returned the pick 38 yards to the Broncos' 45.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That led to yet another score for Harvey.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This time, Nix covered the final 5 yards of their drive by finding the young rusher running free on the right side for the easy pitch and catch.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, Prescott, Lamb and Pickens' days were done.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In case of too little too late, backup quarterback Joe Milton came into the game and promptly led Dallas 65 yards in six plays to the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The touchdown came thanks to a 35-yard pass to Jalen Tolbert, the first for both players this season, to wrap up the game's scoring, 44-24.

text: Game Coverage Dallas Cowboys crumble in 27-17 Week 9 defeat to Arizona Cardinals November 3, 2025, 10:24 pm by Mark Heaney 5 Add us on Google The Dallas Cowboys have fallen, at home, to an Arizona Cardinals team that came into Week 9 at 2-5, and without their starting quarterback.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The final score in this messy, mistake-filled game was 27-17.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It’s the second-straight loss for Dallas, bringing their record to 3-5-1, effectively burying them in the race for the NFC East.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: For a front office that won’t stop spewing about incoming trades to bolster the roster before tomorrow’s trade deadline, it may be time to punt on the market as their playoff hopes continue to dwindle.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Let’s recap this crushing loss by looking at the offense, defense, and special teams performances that led to the final result.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Offensive Disaster: Mistakes Kill Cowboys In Week 9 You don’t need me to tell you the Cowboys’ offense was ugly for the vast majority of this game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The unit did not score a touchdown until Ryan Flournoy’s 4th-quarter grab.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Arizona gave them chances, even kicking off to start the game, but Dallas turned that possession into a turnover on downs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: From there, they had a negative 12-yard, 3-play drive that resulted in a Bryan Anger punt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was his only punt of the night, but only because Dallas’s next drive went like this: a turnover, two field goal attempts, and another turnover on downs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: As I mentioned, the young Flournoy got into the end zone to snap that dreadful streak, before the Cowboys got the ball back when 7:11 on the clock, hoping to cut it to a one-score affair.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: George Pickens hurt things with a 15-yard penalty before Javonte Williams fumbled away their last chance.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In total, the offense had four drives that ended in either a fumble or a turnover on downs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It was a bad, bad night for the offensive line, and a few of Dak Prescott’s top weapons.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Mistakes killed their chances, just as they did in Denver last week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Defensive Mixed Bag: Early-Game Meltdown, Late-Game Redemption

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: While they got going late, nobody can deny that this was yet another wildly infuriating game from the Dallas Cowboys’ defense.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They opened the game by allowing a 3-point, 15-play drive with multiple 3rd down conversions, before then allowing a touchdown on 8 plays.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This was when it became clear that DaRon Bland was in for a long night.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The recently-extended former All-Pro got scorched by Marvin Harrison Jr. for four quarters, and it showed up in the drive summary.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Marvin Harrison Jr. vs DaRon Bland: pic.twitter.com/48FOymoE1B — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 4, 2025

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Excluding a blocked punt, the Dallas defense gave up points to Arizona on every one of their drives heading into the fourth quarter.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Simply put, that is never going to cut it in the National Football League.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The group turned it on in the fourth, and while you could credit that to the Cards’ foot coming off the gas, it was still an impressive showing from guys like Donovan Ezeiruaku, Jadeveon Clowney, and Dante Fowler Jr.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Of course, the late-game improvement couldn’t make up for the early-game disaster, as the defense allowed nearly 120 rushing yards and 260 through the air.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Special Teams Big Plays: Missed Opportunity, Game-Changing Play It was a weird game for the special teams unit, as the usual stars couldn’t pull off their usual magic, while the unsuspecting guys came up huge.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The NFL’s best kicker, Brandon Aubrey, missed badly on a chance to tie the league’s new furthest-field goal record, while All-Pro return man KaVontae Turpin failed to produce his normal juice on kicks.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the flip side, Sam Williams, who has been demoted to a special-teams majority role, sparked the team’s first touchdown with a blocked punt.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Marshawn Kneeland slid on it to recover it in the end zone, which provided some temporary hope in an otherwise dreadful night for these players, this coaching staff, and the front office as a whole.

text: At 3-5-1, who knows where the Dallas Cowboys head next.

text: Game Recap Presented by Game Recap: Cowboys dominate Raiders 33-16 Nov 17, 2025 at 10:30 PM Kurt Daniels Editor of Dallas Cowboys Star Magazine / Dallas Cowboys Game Program Copied!

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Determined to play in honor of Marshawn Kneeland, the Cowboys did just that in their first game back following a difficult bye week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Behind an offense that put the game out of reach with five straight scoring possessions and a revitalized defense with several new faces, Dallas dominated the Las Vegas Raiders, 33-16.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Not that the game didn't begin with a big question mark as both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, the Cowboys' star wideouts, watched the first offensive series from the sidelines due to a coach's disciplinary decision.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But getting them into the flow of the game didn't take long.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Pickens would go on to earn 144 receiving yards and a touchdown with Lamb gathering in 66 yards and a score himself.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Both players benefited from the excellent play of quarterback Dak Prescott, who returned to form after a pair of tough outings in the previous two games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He completed 75.8 percent of his passes for 268 yards and four touchdowns to finish with an impressive 138.6 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: And on the ground, Javonte Williams had a season-high 22 carries for 93 yards, the team as a whole running for 114 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Still, regardless of the offensive fireworks, most eyes were seemingly on the defense in this one as Quinnen Wiliams and Logan Wilson made their debuts after being acquired at the trade deadline.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In addition, starting safeties Malik Hooker and Donovan Wilson were healthy and back in the lineup while DeMarvion Overshown and rookie Shavon Revel made their first appearances of the season after being sidelined with knee injuries.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Thanks to that influx of energy, Dallas generally made life miserable for Geno Smith.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Las Vegas quarterback was sacked four times, including 1 ½ by Williams, and managed just 238 passing yards on 42 attempts with a touchdown and an interception for a 77.3 passer rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Even better, the defense held Las Vegas to just 27 rushing yards on 12 attempts, a paltry 2.3 average.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overall, the Cowboys outgained the Raiders, 381 yards to 236, converted 40 percent of their third-down tries and 60 percent of their trips into the red zone, and held the time of possession, 33:36 to 26:24.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First Quarter Although Lamb and Pickens got into the game on Dallas' second offensive series, things didn't immediately get better.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On first-and-10 at his own 16-yard line, Prescott was sack-stripped by Maxx Crosby with the Raiders' Tonka Hemingway falling on the fumble.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite the great field position, though, the Cowboys defense limited the damage to just a 35-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Finally, the Dallas offense found a little rhythm with Prescott hitting Pickens for 12 yards and Luepke for 15 more during a drive that eventually led to a 50-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Still, after 15 minutes of play, Dallas was back behind, 6-3, due to another Las Vegas field goal, this from 45 yards out.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Although the first quarter might have got off to a stuttering start, by the end of the half, the Cowboys were in control after reeling off 21 unanswered points in the second frame.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The game's first touchdown came on a six-play, 68-yard drive that saw Prescott complete consecutive passes to Pickens for a combined 34 yards, hand off to Javonte Williams for a 10-yard pickup and then wrap up the series with a perfect pass to a wide-open Lamb for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That was then followed by a lengthy 12-play, 79-yard possession that ate 6:33 off the clock.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott completed seven of his eight passes for 69 yards during the series, the last of which was a dart to Jake Ferguson in the end zone on fourth-and-1 at the Raiders' 5-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But the Cowboys weren't done.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Las Vegas dipped into Cowboys territory for the fourth time, but on first-and-10 at the Dallas 31-yard line, Smith's pass to Brock Bowers was instead tipped right into the waiting arms of Markquese Bell.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The safety then returned the interception 24 yards to the Raiders' 31.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Four snaps later, Prescott connected with Pickens, who pivoted outside before making a nifty cut back inside to cross the goal line untouched.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty made Aubrey's extra-point attempt a 48-yarder, but no worries.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: His conversion was of course good.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Las Vegas would add three points before heading into the locker room on a 38-yard field goal, but the Cowboys still entered the break with a 24-9 advantage.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter Not surprisingly, the second half saw Dallas pick up right where it left off.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: First, the defense forced a quick three-and-out, which was followed by the Cowboys' offense methodically marching 80 yards in 12 plays and 7:07 of clock time to the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Prescott-to-Pickens combo again proved picturesque as the duo paired up for completions of 21 and 17 yards, the first of those seeing the receiver run with authority down the left sideline.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, fellow wideout Ryan Flournoy would get the scoring honors and increase the Cowboys lead to 31-9, thanks to a 2-yard catch for his second touchdown of the season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Fourth Quarter Obviously, the Raiders weren't going to go quietly into the night, and three plays into the fourth quarter, they capped off a 14-play, 62-yard drive with their first touchdown of the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: One snap after scrambling 7 yards to convert a fourth-and-4 at the Dallas 13-yard line, Smith threw a quick screen pass to receiver Tre Tucker, who raced into the end zone for the score.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: When the Cowboys then were quickly forced to punt, Las Vegas seemingly had a chance to make this a game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But Bryan Anger's punt put the Raiders on their own 2-yard line, which soon led to Dallas defensive ends Donovan Ezeiruaku and Sam Williams tackling running back Ashton Jeanty in the end zone for a safety.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After Pickens came up with the Raiders' onside kick attempt – because why not?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: – the Cowboys used 11 plays to travel just 34 yards to the Las Vegas 4.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But on fourth-and-1, head coach Brian Schottenheimer elected to go for it, and Prescott's pass to an open Lamb bounced off the receiver's hands, incomplete.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Not that it mattered much to the final outcome.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In fact, when the Raiders failed to convert on fourth-and-1 at their own 6-yard line, the Cowboys were right back where they had been.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But content with their lead, Prescott kneeled down four times, simply eating up clock time.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With that, the Cowboys now enter perhaps the toughest part of their 2025 schedule sitting in second place in the NFC East with a 4-5-1 record.
