text: Game Coverage Dallas Cowboys playoff odds crumble in 34-26 loss to Minnesota Vikings December 14, 2025, 10:37 pm by Mark Heaney 11 Add us on Google In a critical Week 15 matchup, the Dallas Cowboys once again failed to come up with a key win, losing to the Minnesota Vikings in a 34-26 disappointment .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This marks a pivotal point in the season, as the team’s playoff odds are now astronomically low.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This was a frustrating game on all fronts for the team; offensively, they struggled throughout to get into the end zone, while the defense and special teams were flat-out abysmal nearly the entire night.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Simply put, it was a failure on all fronts to come up with a win when it was needed most.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Here, we’ll recap the game in all three phases of it, if you can bear to relive what became one of the signature losses in a season to forget for Dallas.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Offensive Issues: No Touchdowns?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Good Luck, Boys If you weren’t pulling your hair out watching the Cowboys’ offense tonight, I salute you, because that was as frustrating a performance as we have seen all season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: To start, the unit looked good.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They capitalized on a second-play Quinnen Williams interception with a touchdown drive after a Brandon Aubrey fake field goal, and a relentless effort from Javonte Williams to get in the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Quinnen Williams, the face of the Cowboys defense pic.twitter.com/hXK3xzah8T — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) December 15, 2025 They did punt on the next drive, but after that, they again scored 7, this time with Malik Davis.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: At that point, it felt like the offense was good for at least a couple more touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That assumption could not have been more wrong.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After their second touchdown on their third drive, the Dallas offense kicked six field goals , making four and missing two, and turning it over on downs once.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: In short, that just won’t get it down.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite strong performances from Dak Prescott, Williams, and CeeDee Lamb, Brian Schottenheimer’s play-calling woes and an invisible game from George Pickens did the offense in.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Defensive Struggles Continue: Unit Flails Against Weak Offense Again Similar to the offensive side, things looked bright for the defense to start this game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The aforementioned Williams interception looked like it set the tone, and a punt on the next drive cemented that belief.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Unfortunately, from there, all hell broke loose.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Vikings offense scored on their next three drives; twice with touchdowns, and once with a field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: They only punted once after that second-drive punt as well, scoring touchdowns on three of four offensive drives in the second half.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: J.J. McCarthy, with all due respect, is not the kind of guy who throws for 250 passing yards in a game; he did that today with ease .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The pass rush was poor, and the run defense failed to come up when needed most.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: All three levels of the unit struggled at points in the game or throughout the entirety of it.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This was the side of the ball that put Dallas in an early-season hole, and it was the group that likely ended their playoff chances.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Special Teams Letdown: Surprising Mistakes Bury Cowboys’ Chances Who could have predicted the special teams woes we saw tonight, especially after that masterful fake field goal was pulled off early in the game?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Aubrey missed two critical kicks, one from 51 yards out and one from 59 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He kept the Dallas offense in the game with his four makes, and ultimately, his two misses wouldn’t have changed the final result, but from a momentum standpoint, the two mistakes were killers.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: KaVontae Turpin had an improved night in the kick return game, but he still seemed uncomfortable on punts, making at least one key misread that led to Dallas being pinned deep.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: All in all, if you are blaming this game on any one person, you are drastically underestimating how many factors played into it.

text: This may not have been the holiday showdown we'd hoped for with the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders having already been eliminated from the playoffs, but in the end, the good guys came out on top with the Cowboys winning, 30-23.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dak Prescott wasn't in top form as he completed only 51.4 percent of his passes, a season low, but he still managed to throw for 307 yards and two touchdowns for a 97.5 rating.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He also earned his 30 th touchdown pass of the season, which was the fourth time in his career he's reached the mark, tying Tony Romo for the most seasons in club history.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: At times, Prescott seemed to struggle with his accuracy, partly because he was sacked on six occasions and regularly faced pressure.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Case in point, CeeDee Lamb was targeted 10 times but only had five catches for 46 yards, although George Pickens caught four of his five targets for 78.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, the Cowboys' rushing attack picked up the slack despite Javonte Williams leaving the game at halftime due to a shoulder injury.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He had 13 carries for 54 yards in the first half with the team posting 127 yards on the ground overall through two quarters.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With Malik Davis then taking over, he finished the game with 103 yards on 20 carries, both of which were easily personal bests.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Overall, Dallas rushed for a season-high 211 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: On the other side of the ball, the Dallas defense surrendered 138 rushing yards with Jacory Croskey-Merritt picking up 105 yards and two touchdowns.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But the Cowboys held third-string quarterback Josh Johnson to 198 passing yards and no touchdowns to ruin the Commanders' hopes for a comeback.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Where the Cowboys really excelled was on fourth down as they converted all six of their attempts.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Add on a 40 percent conversion rate on third down

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: and they were simply able to keep drives alive, stay on the field and eat up the clock.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys dominated the time of possession, 38:44 to 21:16, while outgaining Washington, 480 to 328.

text: First Quarter The Cowboys' ground attack came out of the gate on all cylinders as Wiliams and Davis combined for 44 rushing yards on the game's first possession.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott then got into the action with a 19-yard completion to Pickens that set up a first-and-goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Two snaps later, a 6-yard pass to Jake Ferguson, who made a nice grab in the back of the end zone, gave Dallas an early 7-0 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Deebo Samuel lit a fire under the home side on Washington's first series as he hauled in a short pass and rumbled 41 yards down to the Cowboys 6-yard line.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But there the defense held the line, a sack by Jadeveon Clowney on third down forcing the Commanders to settle for a 29-yard field goal.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second Quarter When the second quarter got underway, the Cowboys were already at the Washington 23-yard line, thanks in part to another 19-yard catch by Pickens on a fourth-and-1 at the 50.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas, in fact, would convert three fourth-down attempts during the series before capping off the 17-play drive with a 4-yard run by Williams for the touchdown and a 14-3 lead.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Following two lengthy drives, the Cowboys didn't waste any time reaching the end zone on their next possession.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That's because Prescott found a streaking KaVonte Turpin, who hauled in the long throw and then outran the defense for a career-high 86-yard touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Their combined effort tied for the ninth longest pass play in franchise history, and the longest for the team since Prescott and Lamb connected on a 92-yard touchdown on Dec. 30, 2023, vs. Detroit.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Despite the Cowboys now being up 21-3, the Commanders weren't going to go away quietly.

text: They crossed the goal line for the first time with a five-play, 60-yard drive that was helped by a pair of Dallas penalties.

text: Croskey-Merritt got the score on a 10-yard up the middle.

text: But with 4:31 left in the quarter, that was plenty of time for Prescott and company to add to their point total.

text: Brandon Aubrey split the uprights on a 42-yard field goal at the 19-second mark to give Dallas a 24-10 advantage at the break.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Third Quarter Things got a little more interesting when on its second possession of the third quarter, Washington got back in the end zone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A Dallas punt was immediately followed by Crosky-Merritt taking the handoff on the Commanders' first snap, the speedster breaking off right tackle and sprinting untouched 72 yards for the touchdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The two sides then traded field goals.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Aubrey was good from 52 yards but Washington kept pace by converting its own 23-yarder to narrow the score to 27-20 heading into the final frame.

text: Fourth Quarter The longer the game wore on, the more the momentum seemed to be shifting to the Commanders.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Even worse, when Aubrey then missed wide right on a 58-yard field goal attempt, Washington now had the ball at its own 48.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, the Dallas defense forced a quick three-and-out, which was followed by the team's offense going on a 14-play drive that ate up a hefty 7:33 off the clock.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys couldn't get the ball in the end zone, but this time Aubrey was good on a 51-yard try to up the lead to 30-20.

text: The Commanders came right back and decided to kick a 51-yard field goal on third-and-11 at the Dallas 33 in order to hopefully set themselves ups for one final push.

text: COWBOYS 3 things to look forward to in Cowboys' Week 18 game with the Giants Ben Grimaldi Cowboys Wire Jan. 4, 2026, 9:45 a.m.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: CT The Dallas Cowboys go on the road in Week 18 to play the New York Giants and close out their 2025 season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With no playoff berth on the line, no one should expect either team to play their best players for the full 60 minutes.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: However, that doesn't mean there's nothing to look forward to for the Cowboys.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: This game means a lot for Brian Schottenheimer, who is hoping to finish at .500 in his first season, and for the organization, who wants to head into 2026 on a high note by winning their last two games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Here are three other things Cowboys fans can look forward to in their Week 18 matchup with the Giants .

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Extending impressive streaks One of the most dominating streaks in the NFL is on the line for the Cowboys and quarterback Dak Prescott.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After losing his first two meetings between the teams as a rookie, Prescott has won 14-straight games against the Giants.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: With Prescott being adamant about playing in Week 18, his winning streak is on the line in a game where he isn't likely to finish.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys also have a nine-game winning streak going against their NFC East rivals, as well as winning 16 of the last 17 games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The matchups have been as one-sided as can be in the last nine seasons; the Giants would love to stop the embarrassment, but the Cowboys would like to keep it going.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Jaydon Blue gets his shot It has been a disappointing rookie year for Blue, the running back who was drafted in the fifth round to be the lightning to Javonte Williams' thunder.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That hasn't been the case; Blue has only been active for four games this season and has just 22 carries for 65 yards.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That is all extremely frustrating, not only for Blue, but for the Cowboys, who were expecting more.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Things could change in the final week for Blue, who will finally get his opportunity to carry much of the load in the backfield with Williams and fellow veteran RB Malik Davis both out for the game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It may have taken all year, but Blue can erase some of the doubts about him with a good performance in Week 18.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants have the league's 30th ranked defense against the run, and Blue needs to take advantage of his biggest chance to impress this season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A big game could carry a lot of weight going into Year 2.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Cornerbacks stepping up Dallas' defense has struggled all season long, especially against the pass, and now the youth will be in the spotlight for the final week.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The "it can't get any worse crowd" is about to find out if there's any truth about that sentiment with the cornerback group.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rookie CB Shavon Revel and veteran DaRon Bland are out with injury, and Trevon Diggs' release has opened the door for some of the younger CBs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Second-year corners Caelen Carson and Reddy Steward are expected to be the starters, with Trikweze Bridges playing a large role as well.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Josh Butler, who hasn't played all season while recovering from an ACL injury suffered in the 2024 season, has been activated off the PUP list and is expected to get snaps as well.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It might be just one game, but Butler can gain some confidence in his knee by getting back onto the field before building towards 2026.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: It's a far cry from what the Cowboys thought the CB group was going to be coming into the 2025 campaign, but it's a good look at the options for the team heading into next year.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: We've got one more Sunday of regular-season action ahead of us for the 2025 NFL regular season, and the Sunday FOX slate is loaded with games that could have playoff implications.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Five of the six matchups might play a role in shaping the playoff picture as the postseason awaits.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: One of those matchups includes "America's Game of the Week," where Tom Brady , Kevin Burkhardt , Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi will be on the call for the Detroit Lions - Chicago Bears matchup.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Now, let's dive into what to know about each of the six games airing on FOX this weekend.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: New Orleans Saints at Atlanta Falcons (1 p.m. ET) A rare bit of scheduling awkwardness for the NFL, which put the Panthers -Buccaneers game on Saturday afternoon, knowing that if Tampa wins that game, the NFC South champ in fact hinges on Saints-Falcons.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If Carolina wins Saturday, it clinches on that alone.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: But a Bucs win means Tampa Bay needs New Orleans to win or tie, while Carolina would need Atlanta to win.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The division is upside-down in the second half of the season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Saints have won four straight, the Falcons have won three straight, including a combined 3-0 against the Bucs and Panthers.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Receiver Chris Olave will miss the game for the Saints due to a blood clot in his lungs.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He's been a key part of rookie Tyler Shough's 5-3 record as the starting quarterback.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Is Atlanta's late-season surge enough to keep coach Raheem Morris and general manager Terry Fontenot in their jobs?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants (1 p.m. ET)

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Giants have the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft right now.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: A win here could drop them to as low as seventh, and the draft pick value of such a drop is equal to losing the No. 14 overall pick on the old Jimmy Johnson value chart.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Giants rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart had 22 total touchdowns despite losing Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo for most of the year, but his 3-8 record as a starter works against him for NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: So much has changed for the Giants since their first game with the Cowboys.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Brian Daboll was coach, Russell Wilson threw for 450 yards and Nabers went for 167 and two scores in an overtime loss in Week 2.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Dallas' Dak Prescott leads the NFL in passing yards, completions and attempts.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Cowboys' franchise records for all three were set by Tony Romo in 2012 and are technically within reach.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Prescott would have to go at least 29 of 60 for 422 yards to break them.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars (1 p.m. ET) As long as there isn't a Jaguars loss and a Texans win, Jacksonville wins the AFC South and earns a home playoff game.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: If the Jaguars win and the Broncos and Patriots both lose, Jacksonville would get the AFC's No. 1 seed and a first-round bye.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Either way, an outstanding first season under coach Liam Coen.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Trevor Lawrence Clutches Up 💪 Greg Olson on Jaguars finding way to beat Colts A year ago, the Jaguars' defense was last in the NFL with nine takeaways.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Now they have 30 this season, two behind the Bears for the league high, so credit should go to first-year defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile as well.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Tennessee's offense has found itself in the last month under interim coach Mike McCoy.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: After scoring no more than 24 points in any of their first 12 games, the Titans have scored at least 24 in four straight.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rookie quarterback Cam Ward , who had seven touchdown passes and six interceptions in a 1-11 start, has eight TDs and one pick in his last four games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Detroit Lions at Chicago Bears (4:25 p.m. ET) Back in August, it would have been wild to think Detroit was the team eliminated from playoff contention here and Chicago was trying to land the NFC's No. 2 seed.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: These teams met in Week 2, and the Lions won 52-21 to drop the Bears to 0-2.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson is another first-year coach with remarkable results.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Caleb Williams has lots of milestones in play.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He needs 109 yards to break the Bears' single-season passing record, which belongs to Erik Kramer's 1995 season, and he needs 270 yards to become Chicago's first-ever 4,000-yard passer.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Detroit has lost four of five to go from 7-4 to missing the playoffs, and its defense has given up 30.8 points per game in that span.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Detroit's line has dealt with injuries, but running back Jahmyr Gibbs has 37 carries for 81 yards — 2.2 yards per carry — in its three-game losing streak.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (4:25 p.m. ET)

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Rams have the No. 6 seed in the NFC right now, but could jump up to fifth with a win and a 49ers loss.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: That would mean getting to play at a middling NFC South champ instead of going to Philadelphia or Chicago.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Can Matthew Stafford win an MVP with a strong showing?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He has a league-best 42 touchdowns against eight interceptions, though three came in last week's loss to the Falcons.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Falcons beat Rams 27-24, Stafford throws 3 INTS, Are their Super Bowl hopes fading?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The NFL receptions title is a face-to-face showdown.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Rams receiver Puka Nacua and Cardinals tight end Trey McBride are tied for the league lead with 119 catches, with the Bengals ' Ja'Marr Chase lurking two behind.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Either could get to 130 — only six players in NFL history have done that.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Miami Dolphins at New England Patriots (4:25 p.m. ET) Playoff home games were a mainstay of the Bill Belichick/Tom Brady dynasty years for the Patriots.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: From 2007-19, they had 27 playoff games and only three were true road games.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: So, battling the Broncos for home-field advantage on the AFC side is important, but it's worth mentioning that New England went a perfect 8-0 on the road and has three home losses this season.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Mike Vrabel on the Patriots clinching AFC East, Drake Maye’s MVP odds Can Drake Maye win MVP?

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: He has 30 touchdowns against eight interceptions and has done it without an elite receiver.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: The Patriots have scored at least 23 points in 13 straight games and they're 12-1 in those games, a testament to their progress under offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Miami has bounced back from 1-6 to 7-9, and in the first meeting with New England, the Dolphins led midway through the fourth quarter before giving up the game's final 10 points.

subject: Dallas Cowboys
text: Mike Vrabel has a top-10 defense in most respects, but the Achilles heel for New England is their red-zone defense, where they're last in the league, giving up touchdowns 70% of the time.
